## Critical

### CR-001: Recursive worker-home delete follows a path traversal in the meta's tmux_name
**File:** `packages/crew/test/worker-store.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test "removes the per-worker home dir (staged operator credentials)"
**Severity:** critical

The test pins `removeWorker` doing `rmSync(workerHomePath(dir, name), { recursive: true, force: true })`, but neither it nor any other test asserts that `name` stays inside the worker dir. `workerHomePath` is plain string concatenation (`${dir}/homes/${name}`), so a `tmux_name` of `../../..` resolves to `/` and the recursive force delete runs there as the operator.

The input is not the CLI argument. `cmdPrune` iterates `listWorkers(ctx.workerDir)` and calls `removeWorker(ctx.workerDir, meta.session_id, meta.tmux_name)` for every worker whose tmux session is `gone` — a planted meta naming a session that does not exist is always `gone`. The worker dir defaults to the predictable `/tmp/moe-crew-workers` (`DEFAULT_WORKER_DIR` in `core/paths.ts`), `writeMeta` does `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` with no ownership or mode check, and `readMeta` `JSON.parse`s whatever it finds. So a local user who pre-creates `/tmp/moe-crew-workers` world-writable can drop `x.meta` holding `{"tmux_name":"../../..", ...}` and the operator's next `moe-crew prune` (or `stop` on that sid) deletes outside the worker dir.

I reproduced this, contained inside the scratchpad, by importing `removeWorker` from `packages/crew/dist/core/worker-store.js`: with a planted meta whose `tmux_name` was `../../VICTIM`, `listWorkers` returned it and `removeWorker` deleted `sandbox/VICTIM/` and its nested contents entirely. One precondition matters: the traversal only bites when `<workerDir>/homes/` exists, because `force: true` swallows the ENOENT on the missing `homes` component otherwise — and `homes/` exists as soon as any codex or pi worker has been prepared. I did not run it against a real path.

Fix: validate the name at the one place it enters the store. Reject any `tmux_name` that is not a single safe path segment (no `/`, no `.` or `..`, matching the same character class `shellQuote` treats as safe), and additionally assert containment before the delete by comparing `resolve(workerHomePath(dir, name))` against `resolve(dir) + sep`. Add a `removeWorker` test that pins the rejection.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced in an isolated scratch dir: removeWorker(dir, sid, "../../sandbox/VICTIM") from the compiled packages/crew/dist/core/worker-store.js deleted a directory outside the worker home. Reachable from real input: cmdPrune calls removeWorker with meta.tmux_name for any meta whose computeStatus is gone, which a planted meta with a nonexistent tmux_name always is; no validation of tmux_name exists anywhere in packages/crew/src, and mkdirSync never checks ownership or mode of a pre-existing /tmp/moe-crew-workers. Requires local co-residency on a shared host.

**Disposition:** fixed
**Commit:** `30dd1eb`
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** —
### CR-002: Live-run file route serves the snapshotted credential fixtures
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/routes/results.ts`
**Anchor:** `"we skip the manifest check and serve any file that exists under the run dir"`
**Severity:** critical

`GET /api/results/:runId/file/:path{.+}` deliberately skips the manifest gate while a run is
listed in `ActiveRunRegistry`, so during a run it serves any file under the run directory. The
orchestrator's `snapshotRunInputs` copies the whole project context tree into that same directory
(`executeRunCore` computes `contextRoot` as `join(outDir, "inputs", "context")`, and `snapshot.ts`
documents "recursively to `<runDir>/inputs/context/`"). The context tree is exactly where
credentials live: the bundled context prompt tells the agent "A profile directory typically
contains an identity file … and a credentials file; some also contain `passkey.yaml`". So for the
entire duration of a run, any unauthenticated caller can read the fixture passwords and passkeys.

No guessing is needed: `GET /api/runs/active` returns every in-flight runId with no auth, and the
API has no origin, host, or token check (see the separate `createApp` finding). The server also
binds every interface, because `serveViaNode` calls `honoServe({ port, fetch })` with no
`hostname`, and `@hono/node-server` passes `options.hostname` (undefined) straight to
`server.listen`.

Reproduced. I mounted the built `resultRoutes` against a scratch results dir containing
`<runId>/inputs/context/alice/credentials.yaml` and a stub registry:

```
live      -> 200 "password: hunter2\ntotp_seed: JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP\n"
completed -> 404 {"error":"run not found"}
```

The completed-run path is correctly manifest-gated; only the live window leaks. The test
`"GET /api/results/:runId/file/:path serves files from a live run without a manifest"` covers the
intended cases (`screenshots/001.png`, `run.jsonl`) and never probes `inputs/`.

Fix: keep the live bypass but restrict it to the subtrees the transcript view actually needs
(`run.jsonl`, `screenshots/`, `frames/`, `captures/`, `artifacts/`) and refuse anything under
`inputs/`. A deny-list on `inputs/` alone is enough to close the leak; an allow-list is better,
because it also keeps agent-written scratch files out of the response.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced in-process against the real resultRoutes handler: GET /<liveRun>/file/inputs/context/alice/credentials.yaml returned 200 with the credential body while the completed-run equivalent 404d as not in manifest. snapshotRunInputs copies the real .moe-flight/context profile tree, which holds password and passkey files per context.md, verbatim into the run dir; createApp has no auth middleware; /api/runs/active lists live run ids without gating; serve.ts passes no hostname so the server binds all interfaces.

**Disposition:** fixed
**Commit:** `e9cc13f`
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** —
## High

### CR-004: The global_cli prerequisite is never pre-checked, so a missing runtime aborts mid-write and leaves a half-staged install
**File:** `.claude/skills/moe-dogfood/scripts/stage.py`
**Anchor:** `check_prerequisites` — "Confirm the repo side is built before we copy anything into the install."
**Severity:** high

`check_prerequisites` validates two things: that every registry plugin has a directory under `plugins/`, and that every `copy_dist` source is built. It never checks the other repoint kind. The `global_cli` precondition, that `npm root -g`/`@tc/moe-memory/dist/cli.js` exists, is tested for the first time inside `apply_repoint`, which runs from the middle of the staging loop in `main` — after `shutil.rmtree(staged)` and `shutil.copytree(...)` have already replaced live plugin directories.

`fail()` calls `sys.exit(1)` immediately, so on a machine where the global package was never installed the run stops with three plugins replaced, two still holding the previous copy, and `moe-memory` staged unrepointed. `verify()` never runs, the marketplace registry is never rewritten, and the error text ("Install it from a local `npm pack` tarball, or add a copy_dist entry instead") says nothing about the install being broken or about restoring the backup that `main` printed earlier. With `--no-backup` there is nothing to restore.

The result is precisely the failure the module docstring promises to prevent: "refuses to finish if any hook or MCP command points at a file that is not there." I reproduced it by loading the module, redirecting `MARKETPLACE` to a scratchpad directory, and stubbing `npm_global_root` to a nonexistent path. Three of five plugins were replaced, `moe-glass` and `moe-crew` kept the old copy, and the staged `moe-memory/hooks/hooks.json` was left as:

```
node "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}}/dist/cli.js" sync --background
```

with no `dist/` in the staged tree. Running `verify()` by hand on that state reported four problems, all four of the `dist/cli.js` references, which the real run had already exited before reaching. That is a dead SessionStart hook plus a dead MCP server in both `mcp.json` and `.mcp.json`.

Fix: resolve the `global_cli` path in `check_prerequisites` and fail there, before anything is copied. That also makes `--dry-run` useful as a pre-flight, which it currently is not, since it returns before any repoint is attempted. Have the `fail()` path, or an except around the staging loop, name the backup directory and tell the operator to restore it.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** check_prerequisites skips any REPOINTS entry whose kind is not copy_dist, so the global_cli check for moe-memory never runs before the loop; it first executes inside apply_repoint, called from main per-plugin after shutil.rmtree and copytree have already replaced prior plugins, and fail() exits immediately with no rollback and no except around the loop. Traced by reading; main() was not executed because it stages into the live ~/.moe.

**Disposition:** skipped
**Commit:** —
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** Cannot locate the cited code anywhere: .claude/skills/moe-dogfood/ does not exist on disk, and stage.py / check_prerequisites / apply_repoint / global_cli appear nowhere in git history on any local branch (checked git ls-files, find across the tree, and git log --all -S for each identifier — the only hit is this report's own text). No mint/*.yaml source generates a moe-dogfood output either. This appears to describe a file that was never part of this repository's tracked or generated content; code has drifted past recognition (or never existed here), so no fix is applicable.
### CR-005: The provenance self-test cannot fail, because the flag it passes makes the checker exit before reading the fixture
**File:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (corrected — the cited `.gitlab-ci.yml` was removed by the GitLab→GitHub Actions migration, `b0ae97f`; the identical bug survived the move into the `provenance` job here)
**Anchor:** job `provenance`, second script entry, the echo message "self-test failed: the red fixture passed"
**Severity:** high

The job's comment states the reason this entry exists: "A checker nobody has seen fail is a checker nobody knows works, and this one has no live defect to fail on — so it runs against a fixture that IS misattributed and demands exit 1." The entry invokes the checker with a red fixture path and a `--min-readmes 1` flag, then treats any non-zero exit as proof the checker works.

`main()` in `scripts/check-provenance.mjs` opens with a guard that rejects more than one positional argument and returns 2. The script defines no options at all, so `--min-readmes` is parsed as a second positional. The self-test therefore gets exit 2 from argument validation, never opens the fixture, and passes.

I reproduced both halves. Running the exact CI command prints the usage line and exits 2. Running the fixture path alone does not detect a misattribution either: it dies with an uncaught `ENOENT` on `scripts/fixtures/provenance-red/NOTICE`, because the fixture holds only a `PARITY.md` and a `packages/regressed/README.md`. That fixture was built for an earlier checker that scanned README "Forked from" tables; the current one requires a `NOTICE` and takes no flags. So even after dropping the flag, the self-test would pass on a crash rather than on a detected defect, and it would still prove nothing.

Fix: drop the unsupported flag, give the fixture a `NOTICE` whose imported-work rows disagree with its `PARITY.md` `## Map` rows plus the `plugins/` payload the checker inspects, and assert exit 1 specifically rather than any non-zero exit. Wrap the readers in `checkAttributionRegister` so a missing legal file becomes a `problems` entry instead of a stack trace, otherwise exit 1 stays ambiguous between "detected" and "crashed".

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced the exact CI command: node scripts/check-provenance.mjs scripts/fixtures/provenance-red --min-readmes 1 exits 2 with a usage error from main() before reading the fixture. Ran the job shell wrapper with CI_PROJECT_DIR set; the if-then-fail sees the non-zero exit as a pass and the wrapper exits 0, so the self-test always passes. The fixture is also stale: without the flag the checker crashes on ENOENT for a missing NOTICE rather than reporting a detection.

**Disposition:** fixed
**Commit:** `afc339c`
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** Report cited .gitlab-ci.yml, which no longer exists (migrated to .github/workflows/ci.yml in b0ae97f) — corrected the File line above; the bug and fix both live in the new location.
### CR-006: tmux is reported missing on every machine, because no tmux release has a three-part version
**File:** `bin/lib/probes.mjs`
**Anchor:** `probeTmux`, and `extractVersion`'s "the first `N.N.N` triple wins"
**Severity:** high

`probeTmux` does `extractVersion(tryExec("tmux", ["-V"]))` and treats an undefined
result as "not installed". `extractVersion` requires `/(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/`, but
tmux has never used a three-part version: `tmux -V` prints `tmux 3.7c`, `tmux 3.4`,
`tmux 3.3a`, `tmux 2.8`. None of those match, so `probeTmux` returns
`ok: false` unconditionally, with the hint "Install tmux from your package manager".

Reproduced, end to end. `tmux -V` on this host prints `tmux 3.7c`; `node bin/moe-doctor`
prints `[ warn ] tmux / disables: @tc/moe-crew and the using-tmux-for-interactive-commands
skill / fix: Install tmux ...`. I also checked every real tmux version string shape above
against `extractVersion` and all returned `undefined`. The probe cannot ever pass.

The tier is soft, so this does not block `moe-install --apply`. The damage is that
`moe-doctor`'s whole job is to tell the truth about prerequisites, and it tells every
crew user their crew is disabled and to install software they already have.

Fix: `probeTmux` must not go through the three-part `extractVersion`. Match
`/(\d+)\.(\d+)/` (optionally with a trailing letter) for tmux, or give `extractVersion`
an arity-tolerant sibling and normalise `3.7c` to `3.7.0` before comparing. Since
`probeTmux` sets no `minVersion`, presence is the only question, so
`ok: Boolean(tryExec("tmux", ["-V"]))` would also be correct and is the smallest change.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced live: the host has tmux 3.7c, but importing bin/lib/probes.mjs shows extractVersion returns undefined for tmux 3.7c, 3.4, 3.3a, next-3.5 and 2.8 because the shared regex requires three numeric parts and no tmux release has one; probeTmux() therefore returns ok:false with the install hint despite tmux being present, and no fallback branch or pinning test guards this path.

### CR-007: Plugin roster is duplicated into a third list that no gate reconciles
**File:** `config/distribution.mjs`
**Anchor:** `MARKETPLACE.plugins`
**Severity:** high

`MARKETPLACE.plugins` is the list that actually drives `claude plugin
install|update|uninstall` — `lifecycleActions()` in `bin/moe-install` iterates
it directly for all three lifecycle modes. It is the third independent copy of
the plugin roster in the tree, and the only one with no reconciliation.

The other two are reconciled to each other on purpose. `PLUGINS` in
`scripts/mint-plugins.mjs` carries the comment "`checkMarketplace()` below
asserts this list agrees with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, in both
directions: a plugin generated but not listed is uninstallable, and one listed
but not generated is a broken link. Both fail silently otherwise, which is why
it is checked here rather than left to discovery." `checkMarketplace()` reads
`PLUGINS` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and nothing else — I confirmed
`scripts/mint-plugins.mjs` never imports or reads `config/distribution.mjs`.
`git grep "config/distribution"` returns exactly three readers: `bin/moe.js`,
`bin/moe-install`, and `bin/test/doctor.test.mjs`. `AGENTS.md` lists
`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as a guarded surface where "`checkMarketplace()`
asserts registry and marketplace agree in both directions", which reads as full
coverage of the roster; it is not.

Trigger: any add, rename, or retirement of a plugin. The repo just did exactly
that in `15aa668 refactor: consolidate moe-core and moe-everything into a single
moe plugin` and `521de67 chore(tc): retarget the release surface at the single
moe plugin`, so this is a live class of change, not a hypothetical. A name in
`MARKETPLACE.plugins` that no marketplace lists makes `claude plugin install
<ghost>@moe` fail; `doAction()` returns on the first non-zero status, so the
user is left with the global npm packages installed and only some plugins in
place. A plugin missing from `MARKETPLACE.plugins` is simply never installed,
with no error at all. `INSTALL.md` carries a fourth prose copy ("each of the
five plugins: `moe`, `moe-backstory`, `moe-crew`, `moe-memory`, `moe-glass`"),
also unguarded.

Reproduced. I copied `bin/moe-install`, `bin/lib/probes.mjs` and
`config/distribution.mjs` into a scratchpad tree, added `"moe-ghost"` to
`MARKETPLACE.plugins`, and re-ran the shipped assertions. The install plan's
last step became `claude plugin install moe-ghost@moe` and all three
assertions in the "lifecycle action contract" block still passed.

Fix: extend `marketplaceProblems()` in `scripts/mint-plugins.mjs` to import
`MARKETPLACE` from `config/distribution.mjs` and reconcile
`MARKETPLACE.plugins` against the same `built`/`listed` maps it already
compares, in both directions. That puts the third list under the gate the
comment already describes, and `pnpm mint:check` then fails on drift.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** scripts/mint-plugins.mjs has no import of config/distribution.mjs; marketplaceProblems(), which pnpm mint:check calls, compares only PLUGINS against marketplace.json and returned clean when run live regardless of MARKETPLACE.plugins content. bin/test/doctor.test.mjs uses MARKETPLACE.plugins only as its own source of truth and never cross-checks it, and scripts/check-downstream-scope.mjs has no reference to the plugin roster.

### CR-008: Session key can be written through a symlink planted in a predictable /tmp path
**File:** `packages/core/skills/brainstorming/scripts/start-server.sh`
**Anchor:** `SESSION_ID="$$-$(date +%s)"` and the comment "Session files (server.log, server-info, .last-token) embed the session key — keep everything this script and the server create owner-only."
**Severity:** high

Without `--project-dir` the session directory is `/tmp/brainstorm-<pid>-<epoch>`, a path a
local attacker on a shared host can enumerate cheaply (the pid space is small and the
epoch is observable). `mkdir -p "${SESSION_DIR}/content" "$STATE_DIR"` succeeds silently
when the directory already exists, so `umask 077` never applies to a directory the
attacker pre-created. The server then writes the key through whatever is at
`state/server-info`, and the shell redirect `> "$LOG_FILE"` does the same for
`state/server.log`. Both files embed `?key=<TOKEN>` and the bound port, which is the whole
credential for the companion.

Reproduced. `fs.writeFileSync(target, data, { mode: 0o600 })` followed a pre-planted
symlink and wrote the payload into the link target, and the `mode` was silently not
applied to the already-existing target, which stayed `-rw-r--r--`. `mkdir -p` over an
existing directory returned 0.

Fix: create the session directory with `mkdir` (not `-p`) on a path containing
`mktemp -d`-derived randomness, or refuse to proceed when `SESSION_DIR` already exists.
In `server.cjs`, open `server-info` with the `wx`-style flag set (`fs.openSync(p, 'wx',
0o600)`) after unlinking, so an existing file or symlink is an error rather than a target.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced live: mkdir -p over a pre-existing attacker-owned directory tree returns 0 without altering ownership or mode, and the fs.writeFileSync of server-info with mode 0o600 follows a symlink planted at that path, writing the session key into a pre-existing world-writable target whose mode stays 666. No O_EXCL, lstat check or noclobber exists in start-server.sh or server.cjs for this path, and the hardcoded /tmp/brainstorm-<pid>-<epoch> naming bypasses the per-user TMPDIR isolation on macOS.

### CR-009: Title-only dedup merges unrelated requirements across epics and the dedup test blesses it
**File:** `packages/core/test/iterative-development/test_aggregate_stories.py`
**Anchor:** `test_dedup_merges_duplicate_titles`, "Stories with identical titles should be merged, sources combined."
**Severity:** high

`dedup_stories` in `aggregate_stories.py` keys on `story.get("title", "").strip()` alone,
ignoring `epic_theme` and every other field. Two genuinely different requirements that an
extraction subagent gives the same short title collapse into one, the losing epic vanishes,
and the survivor inherits the loser's source citations.

Reproduced. Two stories titled "Validate input", one under epic "Auth" (password strength,
`domain-users.md:12-20`) and one under "Billing" (Luhn check, `domain-billing.md:30-41`),
produce a single `EPIC-001.md` holding one story. The surviving story keeps only the Auth
`i_want` and the Auth acceptance criterion, but cites both source files, so the output
asserts that `domain-billing.md:30-41` is the provenance of a password-strength
requirement. The script reports `OK: 1 epics, 1 stories` and exits 0. The empty-title case
is the same root cause and is worse: three distinct untitled stories collapse to one, even
though `format_epic_file` explicitly defends against a missing title with
`story.get('title', 'Untitled')`.

Short titles collide readily, and `extraction-subagent-prompt.md` asks for a "Short
imperative title" while `owning_story_titles` uses those same titles as the join key
between scenarios and stories, so a collision also silently rebinds scenario backlinks.

The test picks the one input where merging is correct: both stories share the title, the
epic, and identical `as_a`/`i_want`/`so_that`/`acceptance_criteria`. It therefore asserts
the merge is safe without ever presenting a case where it is not.

Fix: key dedup on `(epic_theme, title)` at minimum, and merge only when the story bodies
agree; refuse to merge (or emit a warning and keep both with distinct IDs) when
`i_want`/`so_that`/`acceptance_criteria` differ. Treat an empty title as unmergeable. Add
a test with two same-title stories in different epics asserting that both survive.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced with two stories titled Validate input under epic themes Auth and Billing with distinct bodies and sources; dedup_stories keys solely on title.strip() before group_into_epics runs, so the run produced one EPIC-001.md holding only the Auth story while citing both source files, silently dropping the Billing requirement and misattributing its citation. SKILL.md says only deduplicated by title and the only dedup test uses fully identical stories.

### CR-010: Re-aggregating into an existing requirements directory leaves stale epics and duplicate story IDs
**File:** `packages/core/test/iterative-development/test_aggregate_stories.py`
**Anchor:** `setUp` — `self.out_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())`
**Severity:** high

Every test in this file, and in `test_extraction_pipeline.py`, aggregates into a freshly
created temp directory, so re-aggregation is never exercised. But re-aggregation is the
documented workflow: `SKILL.md` step 4 writes to the persistent
`docs/moe/iterations/requirements/`, and step 5 explicitly contemplates a second pass ("If
stories were deduplicated during re-aggregation, re-run scenario aggregation"). `main()`
does `out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` and writes only the epic files the
current input produces. Nothing removes files from a previous run, and `assign_ids`
restarts its counters at 1 every time.

Reproduced two ways. First, aggregating three epics and then re-aggregating a revised spec
with two leaves `EPIC-003.md` behind holding STORY-0004 and STORY-0005, requirements that
no longer exist; `validate_requirements_index.py` returns 0 on the mixed directory, and
`check_citations.py` then certifies a roadmap citing the deleted STORY-0005 with "OK: all 1
cited stories exist in requirements". Second, aggregating one story per epic across three
epics and then re-aggregating three stories under one epic leaves STORY-0002 defined in
both `EPIC-001.md` (title "A2") and the stale `EPIC-002.md` (title "B"), and STORY-0003
defined twice likewise. The script reports `OK: 1 epics, 3 stories`. The docstring's claim
that it "assigns stable IDs (STORY-NNNN, EPIC-NNN)" holds within a run and not across
runs, which is the case that matters for a persistent ledger.

Fix: make the write atomic against the directory. Either delete pre-existing `EPIC-*.md`
in the output directory before writing, or write to a temp directory and swap. Add a test
that aggregates a large input, re-aggregates a smaller one into the same directory, and
asserts the surviving file set and the absence of duplicate story IDs.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced: aggregating three stories then re-aggregating a smaller revised set into the same output directory left EPIC-003.md stale and produced duplicate STORY-0003 in both EPIC-002.md and EPIC-003.md; validate_requirements_index.py returned OK because it checks each file independently and never tracks story ids across files. SKILL.md documents re-aggregation as a normal step with no instruction to clear the directory.

### CR-011: Eval harness cannot tell a dead judge from a correct STOP verdict
**File:** `packages/core/test/latte/run-evals.sh`
**Anchor:** `hook_output=$(echo "$hook_event" | bash "$HOOK_SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"decision": "error"}')`
**Severity:** high

Every fall-through in the hook emits `{"decision": "approve"}`, which the harness maps to
`hook_should_continue=false`. Thirty-six of the sixty-five scenarios carry
`expected_decision: false`, so a judge that never ran scores thirty-six scenario PASSes at
5/5 runs each. The hook was deliberately hardened to say *why* it fell through
(`allow_stop` prints "claude CLI not found on PATH", "judge call timed out after Ns",
"judge call failed with exit N", "judge response carried no structured_output"), and the
harness throws all of it away: stderr goes to `/dev/null`, and `$reason` is echoed only on
the FAIL branch.

Reproduced twice. Running the harness in stub mode with an isolated `HOME` prints
`Total scenarios: 65 / Passed: 36 / Failed: 29`. Running the hook directly with `claude`
absent from `PATH` returns `{"decision": "approve", "reason": "claude CLI not found on
PATH"}`, which the harness's own comparison scores as PASS against
`expected_decision=false`. The two outcomes are indistinguishable from the summary.

The ordinary trigger is not a missing binary: it is a rate limit, an expired credential, or
a timeout partway through 325 serial authenticated calls, each of which silently converts
the remaining CONTINUE scenarios to FAIL and the STOP scenarios to PASS. The header's
instruction to "Establish the baseline before reading anything into a number here" is
defeated, because 36/65 reads as a plausible judge-quality baseline.

Fix: treat a fall-through as an error rather than a verdict. Capture the hook's stderr,
and when the emitted reason is one of the `allow_stop` diagnostics, count the run as
`decision: error` instead of comparing it to `expected_decision`; abort the suite once
errors exceed a small threshold. Print `$reason` on the PASS branch too.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Ran run-evals.sh with claude absent from PATH and HOME and TMPDIR redirected to scratch, no network: it produced Passed 36 / Failed 29, identical to a real judge run, because the harness only tests decision != block, so the hook allow_stop fallback scores the same as a genuine STOP verdict and the reason field is never printed on the PASS branch.

### CR-014: The privacy guard resolves paths lexically, so a symlink defeats the deny checks these tests assert are exact
**File:** `packages/core/test/tc-governance-enforce.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test names "denies a level-1 read only after explicit opt-in" and "denies an opted-in %s call that reaches the level-1 fixture"
**Severity:** high

These tests establish that opting in yields a real deny on the Read, Grep, Glob and Bash surfaces, and the hook's own header draws the line between best-effort and exact: shell is "a best-effort surface", while "Native Read/Grep/Glob calls receive the exact checks above." The exact checks are not exact. `packages/core/hooks/tc-governance-enforce` resolves every candidate through `absolutePath`, which is `path.isAbsolute(...) ? path.normalize(...) : path.resolve(...)` — purely lexical. `fs.realpathSync` is never called, so `effectiveLevel` and `scopeTouchesLevelOne` compare a symlink's own location against the policy entries rather than its target's.

I reproduced this against a copy of the committed `.ai-privacy.yml` fixture in a scratch directory, with the hook run directly under `MOE_TC_GOVERNANCE_ENFORCE=1`. The literal read of `restricted/secret.txt` denies as the test expects. A file symlink beside it (`notes.txt` pointing at `restricted/secret.txt`) and a directory symlink (`alias` pointing at `restricted`) both produce empty output — allowed — for `Read notes.txt`, `Read alias/secret.txt` and `Grep` scoped at `alias`, and reading through either path returned the restricted content. The Bash-surface gaps are different in kind: the header already disclaims shell parsing, so a glob such as `cat restr*/secret.txt` slipping past `containsShellPath` is documented behaviour, not a defect. The symlink gap is undisclaimed and applies to the surface claimed to be exact.

The test suite has no symlink case at all, which is why the gap survives a green run. Fix: resolve each candidate with `fs.realpathSync` (falling back to the lexical path when the target does not exist) before `effectiveLevel` / `scopeTouchesLevelOne`, and add fixture symlinks — one file, one directory — to the `denies an opted-in %s call` table.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced under MOE_TC_GOVERNANCE_ENFORCE=1: a literal restricted path is denied, but Read and Grep through a file symlink and a directory symlink pointing at the same restricted target were both allowed and cat through either returned the restricted content. absolutePath in the hook uses only path.normalize and path.resolve with no realpath call, so the deny checks never see the resolved target, defeating the hook comment that native Read, Grep and Glob receive the exact checks.

### CR-015: An unvalidated tmux-name is baked unescaped into a generated bash shim and into raw path concatenation
**File:** `packages/crew/src/commands/adopt.ts`
**Anchor:** `cmdAdopt` — it validates `sessionId` against `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` and `cwd` through `resolveCwd`, then passes `tmuxName` to `writeShim` with no check of any kind
**Severity:** high

`cmdAdopt` guards two of its three positional arguments and none of the third. `sessionId` must match `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`; `cwd` goes through `resolveCwd`, which requires an existing directory and returns `realpathSync`. `tmuxName` is handed straight to `readHarnessMarker`, `writeMeta`, `ctx.tmux.*` and finally `writeShim` without inspection.

`writeShim` in `packages/crew/src/core/worker-store.ts` builds an executable shell script by template interpolation: the script body is `exec node "<entry>" --worker "<name>" "$@"`. Bash performs command substitution inside those double quotes while assembling the argv, before `exec` replaces the process, so a name containing `$(...)` or a backtick executes that command every time any per-worker subcommand runs through the shim. `shimPath` in `packages/crew/src/core/paths.ts` is plain concatenation (`${dir}/bin/${name}`), so a name containing a slash writes the 0755 file outside the worker bin directory. `harnessMarkerPath` and `workerHomePath` are concatenated the same way, and `removeWorker` calls `rmSync` with `recursive: true` on the latter.

I reproduced both the injection and the traversal with a script that transcribes `writeShim` and `shimPath` verbatim. A name of `w$(touch ./PWNED-by-subst)` produced a shim whose execution created that file; a name of `../../escaped-shim` wrote the executable two directories above the intended bin. The quote-break variant (`w";cmd;#`) does *not* fire, because the appended command sits after `exec` and is unreachable — command substitution is the live vector. I did not launch tmux, so I did not verify that tmux accepts such a session name for `new-session -s`; on the adopt path the shim is written only after `awaitSessionStart` succeeds, which requires tmux to have accepted the name.

This undoes a property the package states elsewhere. `packages/crew/src/core/proc.ts` documents that "execFile with an args array never invokes a shell, making shell-quoting/injection bugs impossible by construction", and `packages/crew/src/core/shell.ts` ships `shellQuoteAlways` specifically for tokens "baked into a string another shell will re-evaluate" — which `packages/crew/src/harness/codex.ts` already applies to this same `tmuxName`. The shim generator is the one sink that skips it.

Fix: validate `tmuxName` in `cmdAdopt` (and in `cmdLaunch`) against a conservative pattern such as `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/`, rejecting anything else with the usual code-1 error. Independently, have `writeShim` wrap the name with `shellQuoteAlways` and have `shimPath` reject a name containing a path separator, so the sink is safe regardless of caller.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** parseAdoptArgs and parseLaunchArgs pass tmuxName straight from argv with no regex or allowlist; writeShim interpolates it unescaped into a double-quoted --worker argument and shimPath concatenates it into the bin path. Reproduced by transcribing both functions: the name w$(touch ./PWNED) yields a shim containing live command substitution and ../../escaped-shim resolves outside the bin directory. The same value is shell-quoted elsewhere in harness/codex.ts, so writeShim is the one place that omits it. tmux acceptance of such names was not tested.

### CR-016: Derive-path launch reports success when tmux never started the session
**File:** `packages/crew/src/commands/launch.ts`
**Anchor:** `launchDerive`
**Severity:** high

`Tmux.newSession` discards the runner's exit code, and neither codex gate (`dismissCodexTrustGate`, `awaitComposerReady`) nor `awaitPiReady` can fail — all three are documented best-effort and return void on timeout. `launchDerive` therefore has no failure path at all: it writes the shim and returns code 0 with "Worker launched." whatever tmux did. The claude/assign path is fine, because `awaitSessionStart` gates it.

Reproduced by calling `cmdLaunch` with `harness: "pi"` and a runner that fails every tmux call with `code: 1, stderr: "spawn tmux ENOENT"`. Result:

```
tmux calls: [["tmux","has-session"],["tmux","new-session"],["tmux","capture-pane"] x5]
exit code: 0
stdout (shim path): .../workers/bin/w1
stderr (panel): Worker launched. ...
```

Triggers whenever tmux is absent or the server is unreachable, when tmux rejects the session name, or when the exec fails. `AGENTS.md` notes `node:24` has no tmux and native Windows has none, so an environment without tmux is expected, not exotic. The caller gets a shim path for a worker that does not exist and only discovers it on the first `send`.

Fix: have `newSession`/`respawnPane` return the `RunResult` and fail `launchDerive` when the exit code is non-zero, or re-check `hasSession(tmuxName)` before writing the shim.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced against the compiled packages/crew/dist/commands/launch.js: cmdLaunch with harness pi and a stub tmux whose newSession never creates a session returns exit code 0 and prints Worker launched. The Tmux.newSession interface returns Promise<void>, so launchDerive has no result to check, unlike launchAssign which gates on awaitSessionStart returning proof.started.

### CR-017: Bracketed-paste sanitiser can be spliced back into a live paste-end marker
**File:** `packages/crew/src/commands/send.ts`
**Anchor:** `pasteText`, and the test "strips paste markers embedded in the prompt"
**Severity:** high

`pasteText` claims "Any embedded paste markers are stripped first so a hostile prompt cannot inject its own paste boundaries." The strip is `prompt.split(PASTE_END).join("").split(PASTE_START).join("")` — two single passes, END first. Removing a `PASTE_START` occurrence can *create* a `PASTE_END` from the surrounding bytes, and because the END pass already ran, the synthesized marker survives into the wire bytes.

Reproduced with a standalone script that copies the sanitiser verbatim. Input `ESC[20` + `PASTE_START` + `1~/quit\r` contains no `PASTE_END`, so the first pass is a no-op; the second pass deletes `ESC[200~` and leaves `ESC[201~/quit\r`. The bytes handed to `tmux send-keys -l` are:

```
<ESC>[200~<ESC>[201~/quit\r<ESC>[201~
```

The terminal closes bracketed paste at the injected marker, so `/quit\r` reaches the harness as real keystrokes rather than pasted text — a harness slash command executed in the worker pane from prompt content. Prompts routinely carry quoted file or web content, so this is reachable without the operator typing the payload.

The test that names the claim uses `a${PASTE_END}b${PASTE_START}c`, where the markers are non-adjacent and cannot splice, so it passes while the control does not hold.

Fix: iterate to a fixed point (`do { ... } while (safe.includes(PASTE_START) || safe.includes(PASTE_END))` — length strictly decreases, so it converges), or strip every `\x1b` byte from the prompt, since a bracketed-paste payload has no legitimate use for ESC.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced with node -e copying the pasteText sanitiser and the finding payload: the wire bytes contain PASTE_START, a live synthesized PASTE_END, then /quit and a carriage return, then the real trailing PASTE_END. The END-then-START single-pass order lets deleting PASTE_START weld a fresh ESC[201~ that is never rescanned, defeating the docstring guarantee that a hostile prompt cannot inject its own paste boundaries.

### CR-018: Launched-but-unregistered derive worker cannot be stopped by any moe-crew command
**File:** `packages/crew/src/commands/stop.ts`
**Anchor:** `cmdStop`'s leading `resolveWorker(ctx, worker)`
**Severity:** high

A codex worker registers its meta only on its first prompt (`launchDerive`: "The meta self-registers on the first prompt"). `cmdStop` resolves the worker before doing anything, and `resolveSession` needs a meta or an events file, so `stop` fails outright during that whole window. `prune` will not take it either, because the tmux session is alive and prune deliberately keeps live pre-registration workers.

Reproduced against a worker with a `.harness` sidecar, a shim, and a live tmux session:

```
list:  unregistered  codex  codex-w  -  .../bin/codex-w  -
stop code: 1 | stderr: Error: no worker known as 'codex-w'
staged auth.json still on disk: true
prune: {"stderr":"Nothing to prune","code":0}
```

So `list` advertises the worker and prints its shim path, `stop` on that exact worker denies it exists, and the pane keeps running under `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` with the operator's staged credentials on disk. Launch a worker, notice the wrong cwd, try to stop it: that is an ordinary sequence. The only recovery is manual `tmux kill-session` plus a manual directory removal.

Fix: when `resolveSession` returns null but a `.harness` sidecar and a live tmux session named `worker` exist, kill the session and call `removeOrphan`.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** resolveSession returns null for a derive worker in its pre-registration window, so cmdStop fails with no worker known; cmdPrune skips any name with a live tmux session by design (comment: derive worker mid-registration, keep it); cmdAdopt reads the pre-written .harness sidecar and refuses whenever it is not claude, telling the operator to stop it first. No CLI flag bypasses resolveWorker, so all three commands are independently blocked and only a manual tmux kill-session remains.

### CR-019: Worker state, staged credentials and the executable shim default to a predictable world-writable /tmp path
**File:** `packages/crew/src/core/paths.ts`
**Anchor:** `DEFAULT_WORKER_DIR = "/tmp/moe-crew-workers"`
**Severity:** high

Everything under the worker dir is created with no ownership or mode check: `mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` succeeds against a pre-existing directory whatever its owner, and the paths are derived from the operator-chosen tmux name (`homes/<name>`, `bin/<name>`), not from a UUID. Measured on this machine: the worker dir lands at mode 0755, `<sid>.meta` and `<sid>.events.jsonl` at 0644.

Three concrete consequences on a host with another local user:

- `copyFileSync` follows a destination symlink — I verified this directly. An attacker who pre-creates `homes/<name>/auth.json` as a symlink to a file they own receives the operator's `~/.codex/auth.json` (or pi's `auth.json`) when `prepare` stages it. The copy itself correctly preserves mode 0600, so the leak is the symlink, not the permissions.
- `bin/<name>` is a shell script the operator's agent is told to execute. An attacker owning the pre-created worker dir controls its contents.
- `<sid>.events.jsonl` at 0644 in a 0755 directory is readable by any local user, and `pre_tool_use` events embed the full `tool_input` (commands, paths, file bodies).

The pinned upstream snapshot rated its `/tmp/claude-workers` low because every file there was keyed by a UUID. This fork changed that: the credential-bearing home and the executable shim are keyed by a guessable tmux name.

Fix: default to a private path (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, or `~/.local/state/moe-crew`), create the root with mode 0700, and refuse to proceed when an existing root is not owned by the current uid.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced both mkdirSync with recursive silently accepting a pre-existing 0777 directory and copyFileSync following a destination symlink, the exact call shape used for auth.json staging in codex.ts and pi.ts, with no uid or mode check anywhere in worker-store.ts, launch.ts, adopt.ts, codex.ts or pi.ts, and paths keyed by operator-chosen tmux name rather than a random id. The crew README and ARCHITECTURE.md do not restrict crew to single-user hosts.

### CR-020: Unvalidated worker name lets the per-worker home escape the worker dir and be recursively deleted
**File:** `packages/crew/src/core/worker-store.ts`
**Anchor:** `removeOrphan` / `removeWorker`, both ending in `rmSync(workerHomePath(dir, name), { recursive: true, force: true })`
**Severity:** high

`workerHomePath` is plain string concatenation (`${dir}/homes/${name}`) and nothing in `packages/crew/src` validates a tmux name — `parseLaunchArgs` takes any positional, and the name flows unchecked into `writeHarnessMarker`, `deriveWorkerHome`, `writeShim`, the pre-written meta, and finally into two recursive deletes.

Reproduced: with `homes/` present (as it is after any codex or pi launch), `removeOrphan(wd, "../../precious")` recursively deleted a sibling directory and its contents outside the worker dir. `stop` reaches the same call through `removeWorker(dir, sid, meta.tmux_name)`, and so does the `awaitSessionStart` timeout teardown, so a claude launch that fails to start is enough to fire it. With the default worker dir, a name like `../../../Users/<user>/Documents` resolves the delete to `/Users/<user>/Documents`.

The same traversal also mislocates `driver.prepare`'s writes before the delete: codex's `prepare` will `mkdirSync` the escaped path and copy `~/.codex/auth.json` into it, dropping an operator credential into an arbitrary directory.

Fix: validate the name once at parse time against something like `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/` (tmux itself rejects `:` and `.` in session names, so the constraint is not new), and reject anything containing a path separator or `..`.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced via the compiled worker-store.js: removeOrphan(workerDir, "../../victim") deleted a sibling directory outside the worker dir. parseLaunchArgs applies no validation to the tmux-name positional before it reaches workerHomePath, and in launchDerive the credential staging into workerHome runs before tmux.newSession, so a failed launch alone fires the unsafe path. The driving-claude-code-sessions skill frames an LLM controller as the caller that picks names, so the input is not limited to a human at their own shell.

**Disposition:** stale
**Commit:** —
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** Superseded by 30dd1eb (CR-001): workerHomePath/shimPath/harnessMarkerPath now reject any name that isn't a single [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ segment, closing this for removeOrphan too. Verified with a scratch vitest case (not committed): removeOrphan(dir, "../../victim") throws and the sibling victim dir survives.
### CR-021: Operator pi credentials are staged into a predictable world-traversable /tmp path, and the copy follows a planted symlink
**File:** `packages/crew/src/harness/pi.ts`
**Anchor:** `prepare` / `PI_AUTH_FILES`
**Severity:** high

`prepare` does `mkdirSync(workerHome, { recursive: true })` and then `copyFileSync(<operator agent dir>/auth.json, <workerHome>/auth.json)` for each of `auth.json`, `models.json`, `settings.json`. `workerHome` is `deriveWorkerHome` → `workerHomePath(dir, tmuxName)` → `<workerDir>/homes/<tmuxName>`, and `workerDir()` defaults to the hardcoded `/tmp/moe-crew-workers`. So on a host with more than one account the destination path is fully predictable, `mkdirSync(recursive)` silently accepts directories another user already created, and `copyFileSync` opens the destination with `O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, which follows a symlink.

I reproduced the leak with a standalone script (`node -e`, scratchpad only, nothing in the repo touched): an attacker-owned `homes/w1/auth.json` symlink pointing at a file they own receives the operator's token verbatim, and libuv then chmods that attacker-owned file to 0600, which does not protect it because the attacker is the owner. The same script confirms `mkdirSync` does not object to pre-existing directories.

Trigger: any local account that can write `/tmp` pre-creates `/tmp/moe-crew-workers/homes/<name>/auth.json` as a symlink before the first `moe-crew launch --harness pi`. Worker names are operator-chosen but low-entropy, and an attacker can plant many.

`codex.prepare` stages `~/.codex/auth.json` through the identical pattern, so the fix belongs at the shared layer: create the worker home with `mkdirSync(workerHome, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })`, refuse to proceed when `lstatSync(workerHome)` shows a non-directory or an owner other than the current uid, and write the staged file through `openSync(dest, "wx" | O_NOFOLLOW)` rather than `copyFileSync` onto an attacker-chosen path. Defaulting `DEFAULT_WORKER_DIR` under `os.homedir()` instead of `/tmp` would remove the shared-directory precondition entirely.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced under the scratch dir: mkdirSync of the worker home silently succeeds against a pre-existing world-writable dir, and copyFileSync follows a pre-planted symlink at <workerHome>/auth.json, writing the operator secret bytes into an attacker-owned file. The pi-extension source confirms auth.json is real credential material normally kept at mode 0600, and harness/codex.ts has the identical unguarded pattern. The finding claim of a libuv 0600 chmod on the destination did not match observation; the destination stayed a 644 symlink.

### CR-022: Bracketed-paste marker stripping can be defeated by a crafted prompt
**File:** `packages/crew/test/send.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test "strips paste markers embedded in the prompt"
**Severity:** high

`pasteText` strips embedded markers with `prompt.split(PASTE_END).join("").split(PASTE_START).join("")` and the docstring claims this means "a hostile prompt cannot inject its own paste boundaries". Because the two passes run in sequence, the second pass can splice a marker back together out of the fragments the first pass left behind. Stripping `PASTE_START` from `ESC[201` + `ESC[200~` + `~` leaves `ESC[201~`, a complete `PASTE_END`.

I reproduced the transform with `node`. Input `hello<ESC>[201<ESC>[200~~rm -rf /\nyes\n` comes out of the sanitizer as `hello<ESC>[201~rm -rf /\nyes\n`, and the bytes handed to `sendText` are `<ESC>[200~hello<ESC>[201~rm -rf /\nyes\n<ESC>[201~`. The paste terminates after `hello`; everything after it reaches the worker's TUI as live keystrokes, where the embedded newlines submit whatever precedes them. That is the exact escape the guard exists to prevent, on the one code path that carries relayed, potentially untrusted prompt text into a coding agent.

The test in this file only covers the benign ordering (`a` + PASTE_END + `b` + PASTE_START + `c`), which the two-pass strip does handle, so it reads as verification while the adversarial case goes untested.

Fix: strip to a fixpoint, or better, drop every ESC (`\x1b`) from the prompt — a bracketed-paste payload has no legitimate use for it — and add a test with the reconstruction payload above.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced the finding payload against pasteText in packages/crew/src/commands/send.ts and got the claimed output byte for byte, a genuine PASTE_END reconstructed from split fragments. The defect lives in send.ts, not the test file, and is the same two-pass split-and-join defect as CR-017 demonstrated with a different payload; treat the two as one defect.

### CR-023: An unstattable entry in results/ crashes the dashboard out of the scanner tick
**File:** `packages/flight/dashboard/src/scan.ts`
**Anchor:** `listRunDirNames`
**Severity:** high

`listRunDirNames` does `readdirSync(resultsDir)` and then `statSync(join(resultsDir, name)).isDirectory()` on each entry, with no guard. `statSync` throws ENOENT for a dangling symlink, and for any entry removed between the `readdir` and the `stat` — an inherent race with any results-retention cleanup, or a plain `rm -rf results/<old-run>` while the board is up. The throw propagates through `scanResults` and `scan()` into `tick()`, which runs from `setTimeout`. Nothing catches it, so the process dies.

I reproduced it: with the dashboard already listening and an SSE client subscribed, adding a dangling symlink named `dangling-20260102T000000Z-bbbb` to `results/` produced `UNCAUGHT (scanner tick): ENOENT ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat …` within one tick. The same entry present at startup instead makes `startDashboard` reject, because `createDashboard`'s `let lastGrid: Grid = scan()` runs the same code.

Fix: use `readdirSync(resultsDir, { withFileTypes: true })` and skip non-directories from the dirent, falling back to a try/catch `statSync` only when the dirent type is unknown. Independently, wrap the body of `tick()` in a try/catch that logs and reschedules, so no future read error in the scan path can take the server down.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced: a dangling symlink in results/ causes an uncaught ENOENT from statSync in listRunDirNames inside the bare setTimeout callback of tick(), terminating the Node process with exit code 1; no uncaughtException or unhandledRejection handler exists anywhere in the dashboard package, and the file comments acknowledge concurrent cleanup as an expected condition.

**Disposition:** fixed
**Commit:** `a64c3b1`
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** —
### CR-024: SSE event-name field is never newline-sanitized, so a run's identity injects unescaped HTML
**File:** `packages/flight/dashboard/src/server.ts`
**Anchor:** `publishCell` / `oneLine`, "collapse any stray newline defensively"
**Severity:** high

`handleEvents` writes `event: ${msg.event}\ndata: ${msg.data}\n\n`. Only `data` goes through `oneLine`; `msg.event` is `cellId(cell.scenario, cell.agent, cell.credential, cell.os)` and is emitted raw. Those four segments come straight off disk — `DashboardVerdictSchema` types them as bare `z.string()` and `scanRunDir` copies `verdict.scenario` / `verdict.coding_agent` through unchanged — so a newline in a run's identity injects arbitrary event-stream fields, including a `data:` line whose HTML is never escaped and which htmx swaps into the page with `hx-swap="outerHTML"`.

I reproduced this end to end against a throwaway dashboard on an ephemeral port, using the built `dist`. With one benign cell already painted, writing a second run dir whose `verdict.json` carried `"scenario": "A\nevent: cell-good-claude--linux\ndata: <img src=x onerror=\"alert(document.domain)\">"` put this on the wire:

```
event: cell-A
event: cell-good-claude--linux
data: <img src=x onerror="alert(document.domain)">-claude--linux
data: <td class="c" id="cell-A…
```

Later `event:` fields win, so the frame dispatches against the real, legitimate cell id and its data begins with the attacker's raw `<img onerror>`. `esc()` in `templates.ts` never sees this text. The dashboard exists to display results produced by coding agents under test, and it also listens on every interface (separate finding), so the payload lands in whatever browser is watching the board.

Fix: sanitize the event name the same way as the data, and reject rather than mangle. Derive the SSE event name from a character-restricted encoding of the identity (see the `cellId` finding — it needs a separator fix anyway), and strip or reject CR/LF in `publishCell` before it reaches the frame writer.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** publishCell writes an unsanitized event name into the SSE frame while only data passes through oneLine; templates.ts sets hx-swap outerHTML so the htmx SSE extension renders forged data unescaped. A carriage return embedded in an id submitted through the network-reachable POST /scenarios route survives story-card serialization and reparsing, which split only on newline, into cell.scenario and the frame; the browser EventSource treats a lone CR as a line terminator. Same root cause as CR-025.

### CR-025: SSE event names are written to the stream unsanitized, allowing frame injection into the dashboard
**File:** `packages/flight/dashboard/src/server.ts`
**Anchor:** `controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(\`event: ${msg.event}\ndata: ${msg.data}\n\n\`))` in `handleEvents`, and `oneLine`
**Severity:** high

This file is assigned to shard 12, but the defect is only visible from the escaping contract in `templates.ts` ("Every interpolated scenario/agent/run_id/cost string is run through `esc()`"), so I am reporting it rather than dropping it.

`publishCell` publishes `event: cellId(cell.scenario, cell.agent, cell.credential, cell.os)`. Those four strings come from `verdict.json` via `scanRunDir`, are typed only as `z.string()`, and reach the wire with no `esc()` and no `oneLine()`. A newline in any of them terminates the `event:` line early and lets the remainder of the string supply its own `data:` line, unescaped. `oneLine` guards the data field but strips only `"\n"`, so a bare carriage return splits that field too — CR is a line terminator for an `EventSource` parser.

I reproduced the frame construction with the verbatim `esc` and `oneLine` bodies. A CR inside an error stage yields this on the wire, which a parser splits into an extra `event:`/`data:` pair:

```
"event: cell-a\ndata:  title=\"checks\revent: cell-x\rdata: &lt;img …&gt;\r\r\"\n\n"
```

Via the event-name path the injected `data:` line is not escaped at all, and the vendored `htmx-ext-sse.js` hands it straight to `api.swap(target, content, swapSpec)`, so an `<img onerror=…>` executes in the operator's browser. The trigger is a `verdict.json` under the scanned `results/` tree whose `scenario` (or `coding_agent`, `credential`, `os`) contains CR or LF. That directory sits inside the project a CLI-adapter agent gets a shell in, so the input is reachable.

Fix: strip or reject `\r` and `\n` in both fields at the single point they are written. Make `oneLine` a `[\r\n]` replace, and pass the event name through the same guard (or reject an identity containing a control character in `scanRunDir`, which is the narrower contract).

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced the frame split with a transcribed oneLine and cellId and a WHATWG EventSource line-terminator simulation: a bare carriage return in scenario forges a second event and data pair with unescaped HTML, which htmx-ext-sse swaps as markup. Traced scenario back through card.id and asCardId, which has no validation, to fanout/generator.ts, which parses raw LLM output into new story cards, so the value is not limited to operator-typed filenames. Same root defect as CR-024; one fix covers both.

### CR-026: Docker build context is the monorepo root with no ignore file, so an operator's provider keys land in an image layer
**File:** `packages/flight/docker/compose.yaml`
**Anchor:** `context: ../../..` under `services.moe-flight.build`, together with `env_file: - path: ../.env`
**Severity:** high

Compose sets the build context to the monorepo root and tells the operator to supply provider keys in `packages/flight/.env` ("the provider keys are the only thing an operator must actually supply"). Docker reads `.dockerignore` from the context root. There is no `.dockerignore` at the repo root — the only one in the tree is `packages/flight/.dockerignore`, whose first line already admits "INERT AS PLACED … this file is never consulted". So nothing is excluded, and the Dockerfile's `COPY packages/flight packages/flight` copies the directory including dotfiles.

Result: the `.env` this same compose file points at is baked into an image layer at `/workspace/packages/flight/.env`, where it survives in the layer even if a later stage deletes it. `packages/flight/node_modules`, `dist`, and `.turbo` are copied in too, on top of the `pnpm install` the previous layer performed, which also makes the build non-hermetic.

I did not build the image (that would write into the tree and the daemon), so this is read from the compose context, the Dockerfile `COPY`, and the absence of a context-root ignore file — each of which I confirmed on disk.

Fix: add a `.dockerignore` at the repo root, or a BuildKit-scoped `packages/flight/docker/Dockerfile.dockerignore`, excluding at minimum `**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/node_modules`, `**/dist`, `**/.turbo`, and `.git`.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** The compose context resolves to the repo root, which has no .dockerignore; the packages/flight/.dockerignore states in its own first line that it is inert at this depth. The Dockerfile COPY packages/flight packages/flight pulls the whole directory from disk regardless of .gitignore, including the packages/flight/.env that the compose env_file mechanism tells operators to create. Traced from committed files; the image was not built.

### CR-028: Todo web fixture serves index.html as text/plain, so the page is never rendered
**File:** `packages/flight/examples/todo/web/server.ts`
**Anchor:** `return new Response(body);` in the `serve({ ... fetch })` static branch, under the comment "Was `Bun.serve` + `Bun.file`"
**Severity:** high

The static branch streams the file with no `content-type` header. Under Bun, `Bun.file(path)` supplied the MIME type from the extension; the port to `@hono/node-server` dropped it and nothing replaced it. The sibling dashboard server has `contentTypeFor()` for exactly this reason; this file has no equivalent.

I reproduced it with a throwaway server on an ephemeral port that replays the exact expression (`Readable.toWeb(createReadStream(...))` into a bare `new Response(body)`) against the real `web/public/index.html`. The served header is `content-type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`. A browser therefore displays 5,214 bytes of HTML source instead of the TODO app, which makes this fixture unusable as the Web adapter's target — the agent under test sees markup as text, and every Web card against it fails for a reason unrelated to the card.

Fix: add an extension-to-MIME map like the dashboard's `contentTypeFor()` and pass `headers: { "content-type": … }` on the static response. `text/html; charset=utf-8` for `.html` is the only case the current `public/` tree needs, but the map should cover css/js/svg/png before assets are added.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Ran the real packages/flight/examples/todo/web/server.ts via the tsx already in packages/flight/node_modules on a loopback port with the state file redirected to scratch; curl -sI on / and /index.html both returned Content-Type text/plain because the static branch returns new Response(body) with no headers. The todo README documents this server as the sole Web adapter tutorial target, so every web-adapter card run against it fails for a reason unrelated to the card.

### CR-029: Example story and context trees still live under `.gauntlet/`, so every documented command and link is broken
**File:** `packages/flight/examples/tutorial/.gauntlet/context/profiles/fred/cookies.yaml`
**Anchor:** the tracked path segment `.gauntlet/context/profiles/fred/cookies.yaml` versus `DEFAULT_STATE_DIR_NAME = ".moe-flight"` in `packages/flight/src/qa/paths.ts`
**Severity:** high

Flight's state directory is `.moe-flight`. Both example trees ship their stories and context under `.gauntlet/` — the pre-rename upstream name — while every surface that points at them says `.moe-flight/`. I verified each of these:

- `packages/flight/examples/tutorial/.moe-flight` does not exist, yet the tutorial README's tree diagram is rooted at `.moe-flight/` and its runnable block is `moe-flight qa run .moe-flight/stories/01-npm-init.md`.
- `packages/flight/docs/tutorial.md` links to `../examples/tutorial/.moe-flight/stories/01-npm-init.md` and five siblings. All six links resolve to nothing, and all six copy-paste commands fail on a missing path.
- The todo example repeats it: files are at `examples/todo/.gauntlet/stories/*.md`, and its README documents `examples/todo/.moe-flight/stories/01-add-one.md`.
- The tutorial `.gitignore`'s exception `!.moe-flight/context/profiles/fred/cookies.yaml` is dead for the same reason. `git check-ignore -v --no-index` shows the committed file matched by the blanket `cookies.yaml` rule instead; the negation only ever matches the `.moe-flight/` path that does not exist. The file survives in the index because it was added before the rule, so `git status` will not warn anyone.

Fix: rename both `.gauntlet/` directories to `.moe-flight/`. That single move also revives the gitignore exception. Nothing in `packages/flight/src/**` mentions `.gauntlet`, so no code change is needed.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** git ls-files shows both example trees committed under .gauntlet/ while DEFAULT_STATE_DIR_NAME in packages/flight/src/qa/paths.ts is exclusively .moe-flight with no fallback anywhere in packages/flight/src; docs/tutorial.md, the tutorial README and the todo README all document .moe-flight paths that resolve to nothing, including six dead relative links, and git check-ignore confirms the .moe-flight negation rule for cookies.yaml never matches.

### CR-030: Chrome profile name is joined into a cache path and later recursively deleted with no containment check
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/chrome-launcher-helpers.js`
**Anchor:** `getChromeProfileDir`
**Severity:** high

`getChromeProfileDir` does `path.join(getXdgCacheHome(), 'moe', 'browser-profiles', name)` on an unvalidated name. `startChrome` assigns `state.chromeProfileName = profileName` with no check at all; the regex guard lives only in `setProfileName`, which the production path never calls. `WebAdapterOptions.chromeProfileName` in `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/adapter.ts` documents the opposite: "Must match the regex `/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/` enforced by chrome-ws-lib.setProfileName." `startWebAdapter` calls `state.chrome.startChrome(true, state.chromeProfileName ?? null)`, so that enforcement never runs.

The consequence is not just a stray directory. `closeWebAdapter` ends with `rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on `getChromeProfileDir(state.chromeProfileName)`, and that block runs even when `start()` threw.

The name is `moe-flight-run-${runId}` from the orchestrator, and `runId` is `makeRunId(card.id)`, which preserves the card id verbatim. `makeRunId`'s docstring claims "Story-card parsing already enforces `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`", but `parseStoryCard` only checks that `id` is non-empty. `qa fanout` writes model-authored cards whose frontmatter `id` is chosen by the LLM and validated only by `parseStoryCard`, so a traversing id is reachable from model output, not just from a hand-edited file.

Reproduced by calling the real `getChromeProfileDir`: a card id of `../../../../../../tmp/evil` yields profile dir `/Users/<me>/tmp/evil_20260902T120000Z_ab12`, i.e. outside `~/Library/Caches/moe/browser-profiles/` entirely. `mkdirSync(recursive: true)` on an existing directory is a no-op, so if the escaped path lands on a real directory, `close()` deletes that directory's contents. Treat this as critical if fanout-generated cards count as untrusted input.

Fix: validate in `getChromeProfileDir` (and in `startChrome`, not only `setProfileName`), or route the name through the already-written-and-tested `sanitizeProfileSegment` in `src/qa/util/id.ts`, which currently has no production call site.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced getChromeProfileDir with a traversal id resolving outside the cache root to an arbitrary absolute path; traced an unguarded path from an LLM-generated card.id (the fanout generator validates only via parseStoryCard, which requires only a non-empty id) through makeRunId and the no-op asCardId cast to chromeProfileName and closeWebAdapter rm recursive force. The setProfileName regex guard exists but startChrome never calls it.

### CR-031: killChrome SIGTERMs whatever process holds the configured debug port when this session never launched Chrome
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/chrome-process.js`
**Anchor:** `killChrome`, the `pidToKill = findPidOnPort(state.activePort)` branch
**Severity:** high

`killChrome` falls back to "kill whoever holds the port" whenever `state.chromeProcess` is null. But `createState` seeds `activePort: hostOverride.getPort()`, i.e. 9222 (or `CHROME_WS_PORT`), before any Chrome exists, and `killChrome` resets it back to that value on every exit. So a session that never successfully launched Chrome still has a non-null `activePort`, and cleanup kills an unrelated process.

`closeWebAdapter` is reached from the orchestrator's error path (`await adapter.close()` inside the `catch (err)` block), so this fires exactly when `startChrome` threw. Two ordinary triggers:

- Chrome is not at one of the hardcoded paths in `chromePaths` (Brave, Chrome for Testing, `/snap/bin/chromium`, a user-local install) so `startChrome` throws "Chrome not found".
- `CHROME_WS_PORT` points at an occupied port, `trySpawnOn` returns null, `startChrome` throws "Chrome failed to start on CHROME_WS_PORT=... (port in use?)" — and then cleanup kills the very occupant it just complained about.

`findPidOnPort` uses `lsof -ti:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN`, which matches a listener on any interface, not just the loopback address the session was configured for. For a developer with their own Chrome on 9222 (the "co-tenants on 9222" the divergence comment cites), this kills their browser.

Reproduced with `attachChromeProcess` against a real listener and `process.kill` intercepted: with `state.chromeProcess` null and `state.activePort` set to the listener's port, `killChrome()` issued exactly one call, `SIGTERM` to the listener's pid.

Fix: only take the port-based branch when this session recorded that it owns that port (e.g. a `launchedByUs` flag, or require `readProfileMeta().pid` to match), and verify the target really is a Chrome DevTools endpoint before signalling it.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Traced adapter.start() failure (Chrome not found, or port in use) through the orchestrator catch block to adapter.close(), closeWebAdapter and killChrome, where state.chromeProcess is null but state.activePort is always seeded to 9222 or CHROME_WS_PORT before any launch, so the findPidOnPort branch fires with no ownership check. Reproduced the unfiltered lsof -ti lookup against a self-started loopback listener; it returns any listener pid regardless of process identity.

### CR-032: file_upload hands arbitrary absolute host paths to the page, bypassing the context-root guard
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/file-upload.js`
**Anchor:** `fileUpload`, the `ps.send('DOM.setFileInputFiles', { files: filePaths, nodeId })` call
**Severity:** high

`filePaths` reaches `DOM.setFileInputFiles` verbatim. The caller (`executeFileUpload` in `src/qa/adapters/web/tools/page-actions.ts`) passes `args.file_paths as string[]` straight from the model, and the tool description says only "File paths must be absolute." Nothing constrains them to the run's context root.

Every other file-touching tool in this package is confined: `install_cookies` in `src/qa/adapters/web/cookies.ts` goes through `resolveInside(contextRoot, path)`, and `src/qa/paths.ts` opens with "The one and only path-safety guard for Flight. All containment checks go through this." `file_upload` is the hole in that guard. The model can attach `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.aws/credentials`, or the run's own evidence directory to a file input on the target site, and the browser will upload the bytes to whatever origin the page posts to. Page content flows back into the agent's context through `extract`, `screenshot`, and the console observer, so a prompt-injecting target can ask for this.

Not reproduced against a live browser (no browser launched, per the shard constraints); the data path is direct and unguarded on inspection.

Fix: resolve each entry through `resolveInside(contextRoot, rel)` and reject absolute paths, the same way `install_cookies` does. If uploading files from outside the context root is a required capability, it needs its own opt-in root, not the whole filesystem.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced offline: absolute paths outside any context root fed to fileUpload() with a stub page session reached the DOM.setFileInputFiles payload unmodified. Traced tool-defs.ts to adapter.ts to executeFileUpload to chrome.fileUpload with no resolveInside or contextRoot check anywhere, unlike install_cookies which routes its path through resolveInside, the guard paths.ts describes as the one and only path-safety guard for Flight.

### CR-033: Myers trace allocates the full edit-graph frontier per depth, so ordinary page HTML exhausts the heap
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/html-diff.js`
**Anchor:** `myersDiff`, the `trace.push(v.slice())` inside the `for (let d = 0; d <= max; d++)` loop
**Severity:** high

`v` is sized `2 * (N + M) + 1` and a full copy is pushed onto `trace` at every depth. Memory is therefore O(D · (N + M)) with no cap on either input. `generateHtmlDiff` is called from `captureActionWithDiff` in `lib/capture.js` with whole-document `outerHTML` on both sides, and the two documents differ substantially whenever a route change or a re-render happens — which is the case the diff exists to describe. `MAX_LINES_PER_SIDE = 50` caps the rendered output only, not the search.

Reproduced. Two fully-different documents of equal line count, measured with `node`:

| lines per side | time | heap/RSS |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | 4 ms | 2.6 MB heap delta |
| 1200 | 48 ms | 99.5 MB heap delta |
| 3000 | 292 ms | 734 MB RSS |
| 6000 | — | `Mark-Compact ... allocation failure`, fatal OOM under `--max-old-space-size=1024` |

Scripts: `.../scratchpad/shard-015/diff-perf.cjs` and `diff-perf2.cjs`.

The existing suite cannot see this. `test/qa/adapters/web/generate-html-diff.test.ts`'s largest case, "caps each side at 50 lines with 'and N more' footer", uses `before = ""` against 200 lines, so N is 1 and the frontier stays tiny. Nothing exercises two large sides.

Fix: bail out to a cheap summary above a line or byte threshold (the output is capped at 50 lines per side anyway), and/or stop snapshotting the whole `v` array — store only the frontier entries the backtrack actually reads, or drop the trace and emit a line-multiset summary once `N + M` exceeds a few thousand.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced OOM directly: generateHtmlDiff on two 3000-line fully different documents exhausts a 512 MB heap, with roughly quadratic growth from 200 to 2000 lines. getHtml in extraction.js returns unbounded document outerHTML, captureActionWithDiff in capture.js passes it straight to generateHtmlDiff with no size check or try/catch, and MAX_LINES_PER_SIDE only truncates rendered output after the full trace is built. The flight and glass copies of html-diff.js are byte-identical, so one fix covers CR-033, CR-059 and CR-060.

**Disposition:** fixed
**Commit:** `01d4c3c`
**Resolved:** 2026-09-02
**Note:** Fix landed correctly but got swept into 01d4c3c (chore(review): stamp CR-049 disposition) by a concurrent agent's git commit -a race in this shared working tree -- verified via git show that the diff is byte-identical to what this session authored and tested. No separate fix commit exists for CR-033; citing the commit that actually carries the diff rather than fabricating one.
### CR-035: The `type` tool cannot type ordinary text when no selector is given
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/tools/keyboard.ts`
**Anchor:** `executeType`, and its doc claim "without a selector it walks the text character by character through keyboardPress"
**Severity:** high

`executeType` falls back to `for (const char of text) await ctx.chrome.keyboardPress(ctx.tab, char)` when `args.selector` is absent. `keyboardPress` in `lib/keyboard-input.js` resolves its argument against `KEY_DEFINITIONS`, which contains only named keys (`Tab`, `Enter`, `Escape`, arrows, `F1`–`F12`, `Home`, …). Any letter, digit, or punctuation character misses the table and hits `throw new Error(\`Unknown key: ${keyName}...\`)`. The `type` schema in `tool-defs.ts` marks only `text` as required, so this is the documented path, not an edge case.

Reproduced: I drove the real `attachKeyboardInput` export with a stub page session and called `keyboardPress(0, char)` for each character of `"hello"`. It threw on the first character with `Unknown key: h. Supported keys: Tab, Enter, Escape, ...` and issued zero CDP calls. Script: `/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-ZKeown-Code-moe/4556b327-b63b-49d4-bbc6-78cd4f317e00/scratchpad/shard-015/type-no-selector.cjs`.

No test covers this. `test/qa/adapters/web/adapter.test.ts` only asserts that `"type"` appears in the tool-name list and in the `return_screenshot` set; nothing executes the tool.

Fix: route the no-selector branch through `chrome.fill(ctx.tab, null, text)` (which already handles plain characters via `Input.insertText`) or through `humanType`, which uses `charToKeyDef` rather than the named-key table. Reserve `keyboardPress` for the `press` tool.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced by importing attachKeyboardInput and calling keyboardPress with a stubbed CDP send: iterating hello world throws Unknown key: h on the first character with zero CDP calls issued, because KEY_DEFINITIONS holds no letter, digit or punctuation entries and the no-selector branch of executeType calls keyboardPress per character. The type tool schema requires only text and its description never says selector is mandatory.

### CR-036: A max_tokens truncation that carries a report_result call skips the truncation-recovery path and replays an unsigned thinking block
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/agent/agent.ts`
**Anchor:** `const report = response.toolCalls.find((tc) => tc.name === "report_result")`, which is evaluated before `if (response.stopReason === "max_tokens")`
**Severity:** high

The loop checks for `report_result` before it checks `stopReason`. When a turn is cut off by the output-token limit *while emitting the report_result tool input* — the exact incident PRI-2160 records ("run b35d: max_tokens mid-thinking on turn 36 while composing its verdict") — the partial call is treated as an ordinary malformed report. Three consequences, all wrong:

- `stopped_max_tokens` is never logged, so nothing in `run.jsonl` says the turn was truncated.
- `maxTokensNudged` is never set, so the one-per-run recovery turn that exists for this case is not spent.
- The re-ask path calls `pushAssistantTurn(messages, response.rawAssistantMessage)` with the raw truncated turn. `synthesizeTruncatedAssistantStub`'s own docstring states why that must not happen: "a partial thinking block can't be round-tripped (its signature never arrived) and partial tool calls must not be executed". Replaying it makes the next `client.chat` call an API-level rejection, which propagates out of `runAgent` uncaught.

I reproduced this with a throwaway script under the scratchpad: a single `stopReason: "max_tokens"` response whose content is an unsigned `thinking` block plus a `tool_use` with `input: { status: "pa" }`. Result: `stopped_max_tokens logged? false`, two `report_result_invalid_retry` events burned, and the second `chat()` call received the truncated unsigned thinking block verbatim.

`agent.test.ts` does not cover it: both truncation tests ("max_tokens truncation gets one recovery turn…" and "a second max_tokens truncation returns investigate") use `toolCalls: []`, so the branch order is never exercised with a tool call present.

Fix: move the `stopReason === "max_tokens"` check above the `report_result` lookup, or gate the report branch on `response.stopReason !== "max_tokens"`, and add a test with a truncated turn that carries a partial `report_result`.

**Verification:** confirmed
**Verification evidence:** Reproduced against the compiled packages/flight/dist/qa/agent/agent.js: a max_tokens response with an unsigned thinking block plus a partial report_result hits the report-lookup branch first, skipping stopped_max_tokens logging and replaying the raw unsigned thinking block via pushAssistantTurn. anthropic.ts forwards messages to the API unmodified, so this reaches a live API rejection.

### CR-037: Untrusted page text and an unrestricted host shell share one conversation with no separation
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/agent/bash-tool.ts`
**Anchor:** `BASH_TOOL_DESCRIPTION` and `buildScrubbedEnv`
**Severity:** high

`buildSharedTools` mounts `bash` unconditionally for every adapter, and `prompts.ts` notes "Shell access section — always emitted; bash tool is always mounted." The tool runs `spawn(["bash", "-c", command])` with the model's string, in the run directory, with pipes and redirects working and no command allowlist.
