Fix: set `req.setTimeout(...)` (a couple of seconds is plenty for a loopback DevTools probe) and `req.destroy()` plus `resolve({})` on timeout. Bounding the accumulated `data` string would also stop a hostile listener from ballooning memory.

### CR-166: Chrome is always launched with --no-sandbox
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/chrome-launcher-helpers.js`
**Anchor:** `buildChromeArgs`, the `'--no-sandbox'` entry
**Severity:** medium

The flag is unconditional, on every platform, for every run — not gated on running as root or inside the package's `docker/` image. The harness drives Chrome at whatever `--target` the story card names, so the renderer is parsing untrusted remote content with its primary containment boundary switched off. The same process tree holds the harness's provider API keys in its environment (the TUI adapter's own comment notes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is passed through), so a renderer compromise reaches them directly.

`--disable-dev-shm-usage` in the same list is the usual sign that this argument set was tuned for a container, where `--no-sandbox` is the standard workaround for running as root.

Fix: add `--no-sandbox` only when it is actually needed — `process.getuid?.() === 0`, or an explicit opt-in env var set by the Docker image — and leave the sandbox on for local runs.

### CR-167: The observer session writes raw WebSocket handshake headers and frame payloads into the run's evidence directory
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/chrome-ws-lib.js`
**Anchor:** `openObserverSession`, the `method.startsWith('Network.webSocket')` branch that emits `{ event: ..., ...params }`
**Severity:** medium

Every `Network.webSocket*` event is forwarded with its full `params` spread into the payload. `Network.webSocketWillSendHandshakeRequest` carries `request.headers`, which for an authenticated origin includes `Cookie` and any `Authorization` header; `Network.webSocketFrameSent` and `...FrameReceived` carry `response.payloadData`, the complete frame body (the lifecycle comment specifically mentions capturing the LiveSocket handshake, which is where CSRF and session tokens travel).

`EvidenceLogger.logBrowserEvent` appends the object verbatim: `appendFileSync(join(this.outDir, \`${category}.jsonl\`), JSON.stringify(entry) + "\n")`. There is no redaction anywhere in the evidence writer for this category, so session credentials for the app under test land in cleartext in `<runDir>/network-ws.jsonl`.

This is inconsistent with the deliberate hygiene elsewhere in the same feature: `cookieContext` in `src/qa/adapters/web/cookies.ts` is documented as "never includes the cookie value bytes" and records only `valueLength`, and PRI-1605 added transcript redaction for the same reason.

Fix: allow-list the fields forwarded per event type, drop `payloadData` (or truncate it to a length), and strip `Cookie`/`Authorization`/`Sec-WebSocket-Key` from forwarded headers.

### CR-168: `humanType` sends punctuation with virtual key codes that collide with control keys
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/key-definitions.js`
**Anchor:** `charToKeyDef`, the `keyCode: char.charCodeAt(0)` in the `PUNCT_CODES` and `SHIFT_SYMBOLS` branches
**Severity:** medium

For punctuation, `charToKeyDef` uses the character's ASCII code as `keyCode`. `humanType` then puts that value in both `windowsVirtualKeyCode` and `nativeVirtualKeyCode` on a real `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`. ASCII codes are not Windows virtual key codes for these keys — the OEM range is — and several of the emitted values are the codes of control keys that the same file already defines in `KEY_DEFINITIONS`.

Reproduced by cross-referencing `charToKeyDef` output against the file's own `KEY_DEFINITIONS` table. Script: `.../scratchpad/shard-015/keycode-collisions.cjs`.

| character | keyCode emitted | correct VK | collides with |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.` | 46 | 190 | `Delete` |
| `'` | 39 | 222 | `ArrowRight` |
| `[` | 91 | 219 | `Meta` |
| `-` | 45 | 189 | `Insert` |

`key` and `code` are correct, so pages reading `event.key` behave; pages with legacy `event.keyCode` handlers do not. A handler like `if (e.keyCode === 46) deleteRow()` fires when the agent types a period. This also undercuts the stated purpose of the headed-mode branch — the doc calls it "bot-detection-resistant input", and a detector reading `keyCode` sees values no real keyboard produces. Only the headed path dispatches these (`sendKeyEvents = !state.chromeHeadless`).

Fix: add the OEM virtual key codes to `PUNCT_CODES` (or a parallel table) and use them instead of `charCodeAt(0)`.

### CR-169: `fill` rewrites literal backslash-t and backslash-n, pressing Tab and Enter mid-value
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/keyboard-input.js`
**Anchor:** `fill`, the `value.replace(/\\t/g, '\t').replace(/\\n/g, '\n')` normalisation
**Severity:** medium

The rewrite is unconditional and lossy. Any value containing a backslash followed by `t` or `n` is reinterpreted as a control character, and `fill` then dispatches a real `Tab` (moving focus off the field) or `Enter` (submitting the form) at that position. There is no escape hatch for typing a literal backslash-t. The comment justifies it with "MCP payloads often arrive with the escapes un-evaluated", but Flight's own callers pass already-decoded JSON strings, so the transform only corrupts them.

Reproduced with the real `attachKeyboardInput` and a stub session. Filling the value `C:\temp\new` produced, in order: `insertText "C:"`, key `Tab`, `insertText "emp"`, key `Enter`, `insertText "ew"`. Script: `.../scratchpad/shard-015/fill-escapes.cjs`. A Windows path, or a password containing those two-character sequences, is enough to trigger it — and the `Enter` submits whatever form the field belongs to.

`fill` also returns `{ typed: true, value }` with the original string, so the caller cannot tell the value was rewritten.

Fix: drop the normalisation, or apply it only when the caller opts in with a flag, and return the string that was actually typed.

### CR-170: mouse.click falls back to a second click when any CDP dispatch fails, not only when coordinate resolution fails
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lib/mouse.js`
**Anchor:** `click` — the `catch (_e)` around `resolveCenter` plus both `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` sends
**Severity:** medium

The docstring scopes the fallback narrowly: "Falls back to `el.click()` if CDP coordinate resolution throws but the element exists". The `try` block, however, also wraps the `mousePressed` and `mouseReleased` dispatches, so a transport-level failure on either one lands in the same catch and issues a JavaScript `el.click()` on top of the mouse events already delivered. When the `mouseReleased` command reached Chrome but its response was lost — a CDP command timeout or a browser-WS drop, both of which this package has fixed bugs for (`browser-session-reconnect.test.ts` covers exactly that drop) — the page receives one real click from the mouse events and a second from `el.click()`. On a form submit or a "place order" button that is a duplicate action, and the returned `{ clicked: true, fallback: true }` reports success with no hint that two activations were sent.

`mouse.test.ts` does not reach this path: all three tests drive failures through the `Runtime.evaluate` handler, and the happy-path test stubs `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` to resolve. No test makes a dispatch reject.

Fix: narrow the `try` to the `resolveCenter` call and let dispatch failures propagate, or record which dispatches were delivered and skip the `el.click()` fallback once `mousePressed` has been sent. Add a test whose `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` handler rejects on the `mouseReleased` call and assert no `Runtime.evaluate` fallback fires. Note this file is vendored from `superpowers-chrome` (`PARITY.md` pins `782358e`), so the fix belongs in the local copy with a note.

### CR-171: The per-run profile directory that `close()` deletes is composed from an unvalidated story-card id
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/lifecycle.ts`
**Anchor:** `closeWebAdapter`, the `await rm(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })` under "Recursively delete the per-run Chrome profile directory"
**Severity:** medium

`dir` comes from `state.chrome.getChromeProfileDir(state.chromeProfileName)`. The name is built in `src/qa/runs/orchestrator.ts` as `moe-flight-run-${runId}`, `makeRunId` in `src/qa/util/id.ts` builds `${cardId}_${ts}_${nonce}`, and `parseStoryCard` in `src/qa/format/story-card.ts` accepts the frontmatter `id` after only a presence check — no charset or separator validation. `getChromeProfileDir` then hands the name straight to `path.join`, which normalises `..` segments, so a card id with enough parent references leaves the profile root entirely.

Reproduced the path computation only; nothing was deleted. With `id: ../../../../../../../../tmp/flight-victim`, `getChromeProfileDir` returned `/tmp/flight-victim_20260902T120000Z_ab12` instead of a path under `~/Library/Caches/moe/browser-profiles/`. Script: `.../scratchpad/shard-015/profile-dir-escape.cjs`. The same unvalidated name also reaches `mkdirSync(state.chromeUserDataDir, { recursive: true })` in `lib/chrome-process.js`, so the escaped directory is created and populated with Chrome profile state before it is removed.

Scope, stated honestly: the appended `_<timestamp>_<nonce>` means the computed path never matches a pre-existing directory name, so this cannot delete existing data today. What it can do is create and then recursively remove a Chrome-populated directory at an arbitrary filesystem location — inside a git worktree, a synced folder, or a sibling project. The random suffix is the only thing standing between this and arbitrary recursive deletion, and it is not a designed control.

Note that `src/qa/paths.ts` already provides the right primitive: `resolveInside` rejects absolute paths and `..` segments and canonicalises through `realpathSync`. Fix: validate the card id at parse time against the charset `src/qa/api/routes/results.ts` already assumes ("story-card parse enforces `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`" — a comment that does not match the code), and assert containment with `isSafePath` before the `rm`.

### CR-172: Screenshot temp paths are millisecond-granular and shared across concurrent runs
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/adapters/web/tools/visual.ts`
**Anchor:** `executeScreenshot`, `join(tmpdir(), \`moe-flight-screenshot-${Date.now()}.png\`)`
**Severity:** medium

The path carries no per-run, per-process, or random component. `DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS` in `src/qa/config.ts` is 4, and the HTTP daemon runs those in one process against one `os.tmpdir()`, so two screenshots taken in the same millisecond resolve to the same file. The sequence is write (in `lib/screenshot.js`, `fs.writeFileSync(filename, buffer)`), then `readFileSync(tmpFile)`; interleaved across runs, one run reads the other run's pixels and `logger.saveScreenshot` files them as its own evidence. For a tool whose output is the artifact a human reviews, silently attaching the wrong screenshot is worse than failing.

Reproduced the granularity: 200,000 evaluations of the exact expression produced 181 distinct names, with up to 1,180 calls sharing one name. Command recorded in `.../scratchpad/shard-015/` (a one-line `node -e`). I did not race two live runs.

Second problem on the same path: `fs.writeFileSync` follows symlinks and there is no `O_EXCL`. On Linux, where `os.tmpdir()` is the shared `/tmp`, a local user can pre-create `moe-flight-screenshot-<predicted ms>.png` as a symlink and have the QA process overwrite the link target. macOS is not exposed, because `tmpdir()` there is a per-user directory.

`tools/return-screenshot.ts`'s `buildReturnScreenshot` builds the path with the identical expression, so both entry points share the defect.

Fix: use `mkdtempSync` once per run (or `randomBytes`) for the directory, keep the file inside it, and open with the exclusive flag.

### CR-173: A max_tokens-truncated turn containing report_result bypasses the truncation guard
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/agent/agent.ts`
**Anchor:** the `const report = response.toolCalls.find((tc) => tc.name === "report_result")` branch, which precedes `if (response.stopReason === "max_tokens")`
**Severity:** medium

`synthesizeTruncatedAssistantStub`'s contract is explicit: "a partial thinking block can't be round-tripped (its signature never arrived) and partial tool calls must not be executed, so the whole turn is replaced with a short text stub." The `max_tokens` check that applies it runs *after* the report_result branch, and that branch returns or `continue`s on every path. So when the output limit truncates a turn whose content includes a `report_result` call, three things the guard exists to prevent all happen.

First, the partial call's arguments are parsed and can be honoured: `parseReportResult(report.arguments)` on a truncated-but-parseable object returns a verdict, and `buildResult` writes it to `result.json` as the run's outcome. Second, when parsing fails and re-ask budget remains, `pushAssistantTurn(messages, response.rawAssistantMessage)` pushes the raw truncated turn — the exact shape the stub exists to avoid — and the next `client.chat` call replays it. Third, `logger.logEvent("stopped_max_tokens", …)` never fires and `maxTokensNudged` is never set, so the evidence log shows a malformed report rather than a truncation, and the one-per-run recovery turn stays unspent.

Not reproduced: exercising it needs a provider that returns `stopReason: "max_tokens"` alongside a partial `tool_use` block, and the review constraints rule out network calls and running the suite. The ordering itself is plain in the source, and the invariant it violates is quoted above from the same file.

Fix: hoist the `max_tokens` check above the report_result lookup, or make the report branch defer to the truncation path when `response.stopReason === "max_tokens"`.

### CR-174: Reflection trace interpolates tool arguments into the SYSTEM-REMINDER block unescaped
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/agent/reflection.ts`
**Anchor:** `buildReflectionReminder`
**Severity:** medium

`buildReflectionReminder` builds a pseudo-XML control block and splices `traceText` into it with
no escaping. `traceText` comes from `renderTrace` → `formatToolCall` → `renderValue`, which
renders each argument with `JSON.stringify` and truncates to `MAX_ARG_VALUE_LEN` (120). JSON
string escaping does not touch `<`, `>` or `/`, so a tool argument containing
`</SYSTEM-REMINDER>` closes the block early and everything after it reads to the model as ordinary
user text outside the reminder. I confirmed the escaping gap directly:
`JSON.stringify("search </SYSTEM-REMINDER> Ignore the persona…")` returns the closing tag verbatim.

The arguments are attacker-influenceable. In `agent.ts` the trace collects any call for which
`adapter.isMutatingTool(tc.name)` is true — `type`, `type_and_submit`, `click`, `bash` — and the
system under test controls the text the tester is asked to type. 120 characters is ample for a
short instruction, and the injected text lands in the one message whose whole purpose is to tell
the agent it is allowed to give up, which is a high-value place to interfere.

Not reproduced end to end (that needs a live model call); the escaping gap and the argument
provenance are both verified by reading and by the `JSON.stringify` check above.

Fix: strip or neutralise `<`/`>` (or just any `</SYSTEM-REMINDER` substring) in `renderValue`
before the value reaches the reminder. The same treatment is owed to the other reminder builders in
`agent.ts` that interpolate variable text.

### CR-175: First wake_on_idle_log after watch_logs wakes immediately on a pre-existing file
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/agent/watch-logs-tool.ts`
**Anchor:** `buildWatchLogsTool`'s `execute`, which calls `opts.manager.addGlob(glob)` and nothing else
**Severity:** medium

`watch_logs` registers the glob but never primes `WatchManager`'s `known` map. `WatchManager.scan()` reports every match it has not seen before as a new file, and `waitForWake` returns on the first scan when `newFiles.length > 0`. So the first `wake_on_idle_log` call after a registration returns instantly with `reason: "new_file"` and a `path` naming a file that may be weeks old.

The tool's own description promises the opposite: "Block one inference turn until watched logs have been quiet for idle_ms, a new file matches a watched glob, or timeout_ms elapses." The motivating case named in the `watch_logs` glob parameter description is `$CODEX_HOME/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` — a directory that on any machine that has run Codex before is already full of matching files.

I reproduced it: with one pre-existing `rollout-OLD-from-last-week.jsonl` in the glob root and only `addGlob` called (exactly what `watch_logs` does), `waitForWake({ idleMs: 60_000, timeoutMs: 240_000 })` returned in 3 ms with `reason: "new_file"` and the stale path.

Cost is bounded — a single `scan()` pass records every current match, so the next call behaves correctly — but it burns one inference turn and hands the model a false "this file just appeared" signal. Note that `WatchManager`'s own suite pre-primes by hand (`m.addGlob(...); m.scan();`) in the "returns idle when no activity for idleMs" test, which is precisely the step the tool omits.

Fix: call `opts.manager.scan()` in `watch_logs`'s `execute` right after `addGlob`, discarding the result, so registration establishes the baseline. Add a `WatchManager.prime()` if the discarded return value reads badly.

### CR-176: Fanout mode route reads result.json through an unvalidated runId
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/routes/fanout.ts`
**Anchor:** `router.post("/:id/:mode", ...)`, the line `const resultPath = flightPath(projectRoot, stateDirName, "results", runId, "result.json");`
**Severity:** medium

The `runId` path parameter goes straight into `flightPath`, which is a plain `join` with no containment check. The sibling route in `src/qa/api/routes/results.ts` guards the same composition with `isSafePath(resultsDir, resultPath)`; this one does not, even though `src/qa/paths.ts` opens with "The one and only path-safety guard for Flight. All containment checks go through this."

Trigger: `POST /api/fanout/..%2F..%2F..%2Fsecret/failure`. Hono decodes `%2F` inside a path parameter, so `runId` becomes `../../../secret` and the handler reads `result.json` from an operator-chosen directory outside the results tree. The parsed contents are then handed to `generateFromFailure`/`generateFromObservations` as LLM prompt material, and `result.scenario` is echoed in the response body.

I reproduced the routing and the escaped read with a minimal Hono app using this package's own hono build: the request returned 200 with `readFrom` pointing at a `result.json` three levels outside the results directory and `parent` echoing its `scenario` field.

Secondary defect on the same lines: `JSON.parse(readFileSync(resultPath, "utf-8"))` has no try/catch, so a malformed manifest throws out of the handler and Hono answers with a plain-text 500 instead of this API's `{ error }` envelope. The results route handles the same case deliberately (`return c.json({ error: "malformed result file" }, 500)`).

Fix: add `if (!isSafePath(resultsRoot, resultPath)) return c.json({ error: "invalid path" }, 400);`, or validate with `parseRunSetId`/`parseRunId` from `src/qa/util/id.ts` the way `run-sets.ts` validates its own id. Wrap the parse.

### CR-177: Card ids are validated only for path containment, so ids the rest of the system rejects are accepted
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/routes/results.ts`
**Anchor:** `"cardIds can't contain `_` (story-card parse enforces `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`)"`
**Severity:** medium

That quoted invariant is false. `parseStoryCard` requires only that `id` and `title` exist and
casts through `asCardId`; no charset check exists anywhere. `util/id.ts` repeats the same claim
("Story-card parsing already enforces `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`, so it is filesystem-safe and contains no
`_`"). The only gate on a new id is `POST /api/scenarios`'s `isSafePath(storiesDir, targetPath)`,
which is a containment check, not a charset check.

Two consequences, both verified by running the regexes and the path composition:

- An id containing `_` or `.` is accepted on create but makes every derived runId fail
  `parseRunId`. `my_card_20260101T000000Z_abcd` and `a.b_20260101T000000Z_abcd` both test false
  against `RUN_ID_RE`. `decideUpgrade` returns null for such a runId and `serveViaNode` destroys
  the socket, so the live-run WebSocket view silently never connects for those cards.
- The `?cardId=` filter here uses a `${cardId}_` prefix match justified by the false invariant, so
  with a card named `my_card` a request for `?cardId=my` returns that card's runs.

An id containing `/` (for example `sub/x`) also passes `isSafePath` and then fails
`writeFileSync` with ENOENT, surfacing as a 500 from `app.onError`.

Fix: enforce `^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$` on card ids at the one place ids enter the system
(`parseStoryCard`), and keep the `isSafePath` check as defence in depth. Then the three comments
asserting the invariant become true.

### CR-178: Run-file route serves agent-writable files as HTML and SVG on the UI origin
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/routes/results.ts`
**Anchor:** `getMimeType(ext)` in the `/:runId/file/:path{.+}` handler
**Severity:** medium

The handler derives the content type from the request path (`relPath.split(".").pop()`) and
returns the bytes with no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, no `Content-Security-Policy` and no
`Content-Disposition`. `MIME_TYPES` maps `html` to `text/html` and `svg` to `image/svg+xml`, both
of which execute script in the serving origin — and that origin is the one the UI is served from,
since `createApp` mounts the API and the static UI on the same app.

Run directories contain files the agent can write: the bash tool's cwd is `<runDir>/scratch`, and
`qa render` writes `<runDir>/index.html`. During a live run the manifest gate is skipped, so any
such file is fetchable; on a completed run an `.svg` listed as an artifact or observation evidence
is fetchable too. The result is stored XSS against the Flight UI origin, which in turn can drive
every unauthenticated mutating endpoint listed in the `createApp` finding.

Not reproduced as a browser exploit; the mime mapping, the absent headers and the writability of
the run directory are each verified by reading.

Fix: send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy` on this
route, and serve anything that is not an expected evidence type as
`application/octet-stream` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

### CR-179: The solo-run cancel endpoint is never mounted, and its test builds its own app
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/run-cancel.ts`
**Anchor:** `runCancelRoutes`
**Severity:** medium

`runCancelRoutes` is exported but `createApp` never routes it — the only mounts under that prefix
are `api.route("/runs/active", …)`. So `DELETE /api/runs/:runId` 404s in the shipped server, and
there is no HTTP way to cancel a single run: the solo path in `runRoutes` creates an
`AbortController` and calls `registry.attachAbortController`, but the only consumer of those
controllers is `drainShutdown`. `cancelTokens.register` is called for run sets only, so even if the
route were mounted a solo runId would find no token.

The UI already ships a client for the missing endpoint — `api.runs.cancel` issues
`DELETE /runs/${runId}` — and no component calls it, which is presumably why the gap went
unnoticed.

The tests do not catch it because `describe("DELETE /api/runs/:runId")` in
`test/qa/api/run-cancel.test.ts` constructs a throwaway `new Hono()` and calls
`app.route("/api/runs", runCancelRoutes(reg))` itself. The test name asserts a production HTTP
surface; what it exercises is a local mount of the router. Not reproduced by request (the route is
absent by inspection of `createApp`).

Fix: mount the router in `createApp`, and register a cancel token (or expose the registry's
`AbortController`) on the solo path so the route can actually cancel one run. Then assert it
through `createApp` rather than a hand-built app.

### CR-180: Mutating HTTP API has no origin, host, or token check
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/api/server.ts`
**Anchor:** `createApp`
**Severity:** medium

`createApp` mounts every endpoint — including `POST /api/run/:id`, `POST /api/fanout/:id`,
`POST /api/scenarios`, `PUT`/`DELETE /api/scenarios/:id`, `DELETE /api/run-sets/:id` — behind
exactly two middlewares: the drain gate and `bodyLimit`. There is no authentication, no CSRF
token, no `Origin` check and no `Host` check. The WebSocket path bothered to add an `Origin`
allowlist (`decideUpgrade`), but `wsOriginAllowlist` defaults to `[]` (`resolveEnvOnlySetting`
with `default: []`), so that gate is off unless the operator sets
`MOE_FLIGHT_WS_ORIGIN_ALLOWLIST`.

Cross-origin JSON POSTs would normally be stopped by the CORS preflight, but Hono's
`c.req.json()` parses the body regardless of content type. I verified with the installed Hono that
a POST carrying `Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8` and `Origin: https://evil.example` still
yields the decoded JSON object. `text/plain` is CORS-safelisted, so that request is a simple
request with no preflight: any page the operator has open can start runs, delete scenarios, and
trigger fanout, and the attacker does not need to read the response for those to take effect.

The exposure is not limited to the loopback either. `serveViaNode` calls
`honoServe({ port, fetch })` with no `hostname`, and `@hono/node-server` forwards the undefined
hostname to `server.listen`, which binds all interfaces.

Fix: bind `127.0.0.1` by default, and require `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site` to be same-origin (or
absent, for curl) on every non-GET. Both are small changes and they are what make the two file
findings above local-only rather than drive-by.

### CR-181: findCard composes an HTTP-supplied id into a path with no containment check
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/cards/store.ts`
**Anchor:** `findCard`
**Severity:** medium

`findCard` does `join(storiesDir, `${id}.md`)` and reads it, and `id` arrives straight from route
params in `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/scenarios/:id`, `POST /api/run/:id` and `POST /api/fanout/:id`.
Percent-encoded separators survive Hono's param decoding (verified: `..%2f..%2fetc%2fhosts`
decodes to `../../etc/hosts`), so the composed path can leave the stories directory. The create
route on the same resource guards its write with `isSafePath`; this read path does not.

The read itself is hard to weaponise for content disclosure, because the direct hit is only
returned when the file parses as a card and `card.id === id`. But two effects are real without
that: a parse failure on the direct hit is rethrown by design ("direct hit: throw on parse
failure"), so `GET /api/scenarios/<encoded traversal>` turns into a 500 whose body carries the
parser's message and thereby distinguishes "file exists" from "file does not exist" anywhere on
disk. And `router.delete("/:id")` unlinks `join(storiesDir, entry.filename)` where `filename` is
the same unchecked `${id}.md`, so a traversal that does resolve to a valid card file deletes
outside the stories directory.

Not reproduced end to end; the param decoding and the path composition were each verified
directly.

Fix: reject any `id` that is not a single safe path segment at the top of `findCard`, and return
undefined rather than throwing when the direct hit does not parse as a card at all.

### CR-182: findCard reads an attacker-chosen path from a route parameter
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/cards/store.ts`
**Anchor:** `findCard`
**Severity:** medium

`findCard` joins its `id` argument into `<stories>/<id>.md` and calls `readFileSync` with no containment check. Every id-bearing route passes `c.req.param("id")` straight in: the scenario read, update, delete and approve handlers, and `POST /api/run/:id`. Hono percent-decodes path parameters, so an encoded traversal escapes the stories directory.

I reproduced this against `createApp`. `GET /api/scenarios/..%2Fgarbage`, where `garbage.md` sits one level above the stories directory, returns `500 {"error":"internal","message":"Story card missing required field: id"}` — the file outside the root was opened and parsed. `GET /api/scenarios/..%2Fsecret`, where the sibling file does parse as a card, returns 404, because the frontmatter id cannot equal the traversal string. `POST /api/run/..%2Fgarbage` behaves identically.

Content does not leak, since the direct hit is discarded unless `card.id === id`. What remains is a filesystem oracle (404 for absent-or-parseable, 500 for present-and-unparseable, distinguishable for any `.md` path on the host), an unhandled 500 on a shaped request, and an unbounded read of an arbitrary caller-chosen `.md` file into memory.

`POST /api/scenarios` already does the right thing: it composes `targetPath` and rejects on `!isSafePath(storiesDir, targetPath)`. Fix: apply the same guard inside `findCard`, so every caller inherits it instead of one route holding the only check.

### CR-183: `qa run` exits 0 on a failing verdict while `qa batch` on the same card exits 1
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/cli/run.ts`
**Anchor:** `run`
**Severity:** medium

`run` is declared `Promise<void>` and returns no status. Its only `process.exit` is `if (cancelToken.cancelled) process.exit(130)`. In the multi-pass branch it awaits `handle.completion` into `setResult` and uses `setResult.summary` for display only. `qaMain`'s `case "run"` therefore awaits and breaks, so the process exits 0 regardless of verdict. `case "batch"` does `if (exitCode !== 0) process.exit(exitCode)`, and `runBatch` returns 1 for any non-pass.

I reproduced the divergence with a scripted client. One card, one `report("fail", …)`: `run(...)` resolved `undefined` with `result.json` on disk carrying `"status": "fail"`, while `runBatch(...)` over the same card and the same scripted verdict returned exit code 1. So `moe-flight qa run card.md` reports success for a failing acceptance test, and the recommended workaround is to invoke `batch` with a single card.

`test/qa/cli/run.test.ts` leaves this unguarded: both of its tests script only `report("pass", …)` and neither inspects an exit status, so no verdict other than pass is exercised through this command at any pass count.

Fix: have `run` return an exit code derived the way `runBatch` derives its own (0 iff every attempt is `pass`) and propagate it from `qaMain`, or state the divergence explicitly in the usage text so `run` is not mistaken for a CI gate.

### CR-184: The show-prompt introspection command omits fetch_credential from the tool list it claims is exact
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/cli/show-prompt.ts`
**Anchor:** `adapterForIntrospect`, and the comment "Honest introspection: instantiate the actual adapter (no start()) so tool list and describeTarget() match what the agent receives"
**Severity:** medium

`adapterForIntrospect` constructs each adapter with `{ contextRoot }` only. `buildSharedTools` registers `fetch_credential` iff it is handed a `credentialResolver` and the context root is populated, so the introspection view drops that tool whenever `MOE_FLIGHT_CREDENTIAL_RESOLVER` is set — the one configuration where an operator most wants to confirm what the agent can reach. `ShowPromptOptions` has no field to thread the resolver through, and `qa index.ts` does not pass one, so the omission is structural rather than a missed call site.

I reproduced it by building two `WebAdapter` instances, one as `adapterForIntrospect` does and one as a real run does, and diffing `toolDefinitions()`: the introspection instance is missing exactly `fetch_credential`.

The same constructor also omits `runDir`, so the `bash` tool is built with `cwd: undefined` rather than the run's scratch directory. Fix: add `credentialResolver` to `ShowPromptOptions`, pass `config.credentialResolver` from the dispatch site, and hand `adapterForIntrospect` a representative run directory.

### CR-185: Tool-call argument bodies are never length-capped, so a wide call corrupts the inline-rewrite display
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/cli/stream/pretty.ts`
**Anchor:** `renderToolCall` setting `this.pendingRewrite = { base }`, consumed by `renderToolResult`'s `this.sink.write("\x1b[1A\x1b[2K")`
**Severity:** medium

In color mode `renderToolCall` writes the call line plus a trailing `⋯`, and `renderToolResult` erases it with one cursor-up and one erase-line before rewriting. That contract holds only while the call line occupies a single physical terminal row. Nothing enforces that. `formatToolArgs` falls back to `JSON.stringify(args)` for any tool without a humanizer, and `jsonFallback` applies no cap — despite the module's own docstring saying the fallback is "truncated by the caller". `truncateArgs` exists in `wrap.ts` for exactly this and is called from nowhere in `src/`, only from `test/qa/cli/stream/wrap.test.ts`.

Twelve tools have humanizers; the live catalogue has twenty-five. `bash`, `extract`, `type_and_submit`, `file_upload`, `drag`, `scroll`, `watch_logs` and `install_passkey` all take the uncapped path. I reproduced a `bash` call whose rendered line is 136 visible characters at `columns: 100` while the renderer emits a single `\x1b[1A`; the erase lands on the wrapped continuation, so the first physical row survives on screen as an orphaned fragment.

Note that two of the twelve humanizer keys, `wait_for_selector` and `install_storage`, match no tool in the catalogue, so they are dead entries.

Fix: apply `truncateArgs(body, columns - overhead)` in `renderToolCall`, and either measure the emitted width to choose the cursor-up count or drop the rewrite when the line would wrap.

### CR-186: Credential resolver stderr is written to the transcript verbatim on the failure path
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/context/credential-tool.ts`
**Anchor:** `case "nonzero_exit"` returning `textResult(\`Error: fetch_credential resolver exited ${result.exitCode} for ${entity}:${key}:\n${result.stderr}\`)`
**Severity:** medium

The success path is careful: it returns `textResult(result.stdout, { transcriptText: "<credential redacted: ...>" })` so `run.jsonl` records only a marker unless the operator opts in with `MOE_FLIGHT_CREDENTIAL_INCLUDE_IN_TRANSCRIPTS`. The `nonzero_exit` path interpolates the resolver's entire stderr into the returned text and passes no `transcriptText`, so `EvidenceLogger.logToolResult` records those bytes as `tool_result.text` in `run.jsonl` regardless of the opt-in. Real resolvers print diagnostics to stderr — vault errors, token echoes, curl traces — and those are exactly the bytes the redaction control was added to keep out of archived transcripts. `docs/credentials.md` states "The action log records only `entity`, `key`, exit code, stdout length, stderr length, elapsed ms — never the bytes", which holds for the `fetch_credential_failed` event but not for the tool-result row.

I reproduced it with a resolver that exits 3 after printing a fake vault token to stderr: the returned result carried the token in `text` with `transcriptText: undefined`, while the same tool against a succeeding resolver produced the redaction marker.

The `timeout` case has the same shape but does not interpolate stderr, so only `nonzero_exit` leaks. Fix: cap and redact stderr in the transcript copy — return the prose to the agent but pass a `transcriptText` that carries only the step, exit code and stderr length, matching the event payload.

### CR-187: Context tree follows symlinks out of the context root and advertises files the read tool then refuses
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/context/tree.ts`
**Anchor:** `listVisibleEntries` uses `statSync`, and `walk` recurses on any `entry.isDirectory`
**Severity:** medium

`listVisibleEntries` stats with `statSync`, which follows symlinks, and `walk` recurses into anything that reports as a directory. A symlink inside `.moe-flight/context/` pointing outside the root is therefore walked, and its contents are rendered into the system prompt's Context section. `read-tool.ts` resolves through `resolveInside`, which canonicalizes with `realpathSync` and rejects anything outside the root. The two disagree.

I reproduced it: a context root containing `vendor -> <outside dir>` renders `vendor/ secrets/ keys.md (10 bytes)` into the prompt, and `read({path: "vendor/secrets/keys.md"})` returns `Error: path "vendor/secrets/keys.md" escapes the context root`.

Two consequences. The agent is told the tree "is the full map of what's available" (the `read` tool description) and then cannot read part of it, which burns turns on a dead end. And the names and byte sizes of files outside the context root are shipped to the model provider in the prompt, which the containment guard in `paths.ts` exists precisely to prevent.

Fix: have `listVisibleEntries` use `lstatSync` and skip symlinks, or canonicalize each candidate and drop anything `isSafePath` rejects, so the tree and the `read` tool enforce the same boundary. Separately, the entry and byte budgets bound only the emitted lines, not the walk — once `truncated` is set the walk continues purely to increment `remaining`, so a large or symlink-widened tree is traversed in full.

### CR-188: Context-tree budget bounds the output but not the walk, so one symlink costs ten seconds
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/context/tree.ts`
**Anchor:** `walk` — "Already over budget — count the rest and do not emit."
**Severity:** medium

Once either budget trips, `walk` keeps recursing through the entire reachable tree so the truncation line can name an exact count. `listVisibleEntries` uses `statSync`, which follows symlinks, and there is no depth cap and no visited-inode set. So the cost of rendering the context tree is O(everything reachable from `contextRoot`), independent of `maxBytes` and `maxEntries`.

Reproduced. With a context directory holding one symlink to a large real tree and options `{ maxEntries: 5, maxBytes: 200 }`, `renderContextTree` returned 6 output lines after walking 211,859 entries in 10,040 ms. This runs synchronously on the main thread, once per run at turn 0, before the agent starts. A symlink cycle is bounded only accidentally: I confirmed a `a/loop -> ../a` cycle terminates because the kernel returns ELOOP at about 32 levels, which `listVisibleEntries` swallows — but it renders ~30 phantom directory lines first and reports them in the truncation count.

The two truncation tests use ten flat files, so neither exercises post-budget cost, and no test uses a symlink at all.

Fix: stop the walk when `truncated` becomes true and render `... (truncated: N or more entries ...)`, or keep the exact count but cap the walk with a depth limit and a visited-realpath set. Skipping symlinked directories outright would also match the `read` tool, which already rejects any path whose realpath leaves the context root.

### CR-189: Fanout silently merges generated cards into one when the model puts `title:` before `id:`
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/fanout/generator.ts`
**Anchor:** `splitAndValidateCards`'s fallback `chunks = stripped.split(/\n(?=---\nid:)/)`
**Severity:** medium

When the model omits the requested `---CARD---` markers, the fallback splits on frontmatter boundaries — but the lookahead requires `id:` to be the *first* key in the block. If the model emits `title:` first, no split point matches, the whole response becomes one chunk, and `parseStoryCard`'s non-greedy `/^---\n([\s\S]*?)\n---\n?([\s\S]*)$/` happily parses the first block's frontmatter with every later card absorbed into the description. The function returns one valid-looking card and logs nothing, because the `console.error` path only fires on a parse *failure*.

Reproduced with a scratchpad script calling `splitAndValidateCards` on the same two-card text twice, once with `id:` first and once with `title:` first:

```
id: first:      2 card(s) returned
title: first:   1 card(s) returned  (one 314-char blob)
```

Key ordering in generated YAML is not something the caller can rely on, and the loss is silent rather than an error.

Fix: match the frontmatter boundary without pinning the key, e.g. split on `/\n(?=---\n)/` and let `parseStoryCard` reject non-card chunks (it already does), or scan the frontmatter block for an `id:` line on any line.

### CR-190: Fanout card splitting requires `id:` to be the first frontmatter key, and silently swallows the rest
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/fanout/generator.ts`
**Anchor:** `splitAndValidateCards` — `chunks = stripped.split(/\n(?=---\nid:)/)`
**Severity:** medium

When the model omits the `---CARD---` separator, the fallback splits on `/\n(?=---\nid:)/`, which only matches when `id` is the very first key inside the frontmatter block. Nothing enforces that order: `parseStoryCard`'s `splitFrontmatter` reads keys in any order, and the prompt merely asks for a shape.

Reproduced with two otherwise valid cards whose frontmatter starts with `title:` instead of `id:` and no separator between them. `splitAndValidateCards` returned **one** card. `parseStoryCard` accepted the merged text (it reads only the first frontmatter block), so the validity filter kept it, and card B's entire raw text — frontmatter delimiters included — ended up inside card A's description. The second variation is lost and the surviving one is corrupt, with no error and no log line, because the chunk parsed successfully.

The test `"falls back to frontmatter splitting when no separator"` uses `id` first in both cards, so it never touches the ordering dependency.

Fix: split on a frontmatter-start lookahead that does not assume key order, for example `/\n(?=---\n[a-zA-Z_-]+:)/`, and reject a chunk that contains more than one frontmatter block instead of parsing only its first.

### CR-191: Story-card ids are never charset-validated, so a valid card produces a runId no route can parse
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/format/story-card.ts`
**Anchor:** `parseStoryCard`
**Severity:** medium

`makeRunId` in `src/qa/util/id.ts` documents a load-bearing invariant: "The cardId is preserved verbatim. Story-card parsing already enforces `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`, so it is filesystem-safe and contains no `_`, which makes the `_` separator unambiguous." That claim is false. `parseStoryCard` checks only that `id` and `title` are non-empty; it applies no pattern. `POST /api/scenarios` gates the id with `isSafePath` alone, which accepts anything that stays inside the stories directory.

I reproduced the consequence with a throwaway script driving `createApp`. `POST /api/scenarios` with `{"id":"foo_bar","title":"Underscore card"}` returns 201 and the card round-trips through `GET /api/scenarios/foo_bar`. `makeRunId("foo_bar")` then yields `foo_bar_20260902T145546Z_kgdw`, and `parseRunId` on that string returns `null` because its `[a-zA-Z0-9-]+` card segment cannot match `foo_bar`. `decideUpgrade` for `/api/ws?run=<that runId>` therefore returns `null`, and `serveViaNode` destroys the socket. The run executes and writes results, but its live WebSocket channel can never be opened: no progress, no frames, no transcript snapshot. The same script showed `with space`, `dot.dot`, `UPPER_case` and `emoji-❤` all accepted as ids, and `a/b` accepted by `isSafePath` and then crashing `writeFileSync` with an unhandled `ENOENT`.

Nothing in this shard guards the invariant. `test/qa/api/run.test.ts` asserts the runId shape with `/^story-001_\d{8}T\d{6}Z_[a-z0-9]{4}$/`, which only holds because the fixture id happens to be well-formed.

Fix: enforce `/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$/` on `id` inside `parseStoryCard` and on the create-route body, so the invariant `makeRunId` and `parseRunId` both depend on is actually established.

### CR-192: `qa run` exits 0 for a failing story while `qa batch` exits 1
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/index.ts`
**Anchor:** `qaMain`'s `case "run"` (`await run({...}); break;`) next to `case "batch"` (`if (exitCode !== 0) process.exit(exitCode);`)
**Severity:** medium

`runBatch` returns an exit code derived from the run set's statuses — "return anyNonPass === 0 ? 0 : 1" — and `qaMain` propagates it. `run` returns `void`. Neither of its paths maps a verdict to an exit status: the single-pass path just prints, and the multi-pass path only does `if (cancelToken.cancelled) process.exit(130)`. So `moe-flight qa run story.md` reports success to the shell whether the acceptance criteria passed, failed, or errored, while the sibling command with the same job reports failure. Nothing in the package documents an intentional asymmetry, and no test covers `run`'s exit code (`test/qa/cli/batch.test.ts` covers `runBatch`'s).

Anyone scripting the primary command in CI silently gets a green build for a failing story.

Fix: have `run` return a code the way `runBatch` does, using the same non-pass rule, and propagate it from `qaMain`.

### CR-193: Every Anthropic request sends adaptive thinking, so the legacy-model token caps can never apply
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/models/anthropic.ts`
**Anchor:** `createAnthropicClient`'s `chat` sending `output_config: { effort: "medium" }` and `thinking: { type: "adaptive" }` unconditionally, versus `maxOutputTokensForModel`
**Severity:** medium

`maxOutputTokensForModel` branches deliberately for older families — `/^claude-3-[57]-/` gets 8192 and "Claude 3.0, Claude 2.x, and any unrecognized id" gets 4096 — and `test/qa/models/anthropic.test.ts` pins those values for `claude-3-opus-20240229`, `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` and `claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219`. `resolveProvider` routes any `claude*` id here, and no allowlist blocks those ids by default (`models.available` is empty unless the operator sets `MOE_FLIGHT_MODELS`). But the same request body always carries adaptive thinking and an effort setting, which those model generations reject, so a run configured with any of them fails at the first API call and the computed cap is never used.

The unit tests pass while the behaviour they imply is unreachable, because they exercise the pure helper and never the request body.

Fix: make `thinking` and `output_config` model-aware in the same place the cap is decided (omit both for `claude-3-*` and `claude-2-*`), or drop the legacy branches and reject those ids up front in `resolveProvider` so the failure is a clear message rather than a provider 400.

### CR-194: Escaping only `</script` lets report data swallow the rest of the HTML page
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/render/render-run.ts`
**Anchor:** `renderRunFromTemplate` and the comment "Escape any </script in the JSON to prevent breaking out of the surrounding <script> tag."
**Severity:** medium

The payload is escaped with `.replace(/<\/script/gi, "<\\/script")` only. That blocks the closing-tag route but leaves `<!--` and an opening `<script` untouched. In HTML's tokenizer, `<!--` inside a script element enters the script-data-escaped state and a following `<script` enters the double-escaped state, in which the template's own `</script>` no longer terminates the element. The script element then absorbs the remainder of the document.

Reproduced with `parse5` against a template shaped like the real one. With a benign payload the parsed DOM contains both `__MOE_FLIGHT_RUN__` and the following `<h1 id="after">`; with `result.summary` set to `<!--<script>` only `__MOE_FLIGHT_RUN__` survives, so everything after the data island is gone and `JSON.parse` of the element's text would also fail. Full markup injection is not reachable, because any literal `</script>` the payload needs is escaped.

The trigger is any run whose `result.json` or `run.jsonl` carries that byte sequence, which is ordinary for this tool: the CLI and TUI adapters record raw terminal output, so a story that runs `cat index.html` or `curl` puts commented-out script tags straight into the transcript.

Fix: replace every `<` in the serialized JSON with its six-character JSON unicode escape (backslash, u, 0, 0, 3, c), which parses identically, instead of pattern-matching one tag form.

### CR-195: Static-payload escaping misses the HTML-comment double-escape, so page-derived transcript text can swallow the report's hydration script
**File:** `packages/flight/src/qa/render/render-run.ts`
**Anchor:** `JSON.stringify(payload).replace(/<\/script/gi, "<\\/script")` and the comment "JSON.stringify handles other concerns"
**Severity:** medium

This file is outside my assigned list; I read it because it produces the payload that `useTranscript`'s static branch and `getStaticRunPayload` consume, and the escaping contract is what makes that branch safe. Reporting it here so it is not lost.

The replace covers `</script` but not the other sequence the HTML tokenizer recognises inside raw-text elements. A payload containing `<!--` followed by `<script` puts the tokenizer into the script-data-double-escaped state, where the payload element's own closing `</script>` is emitted as text instead of ending the element. Parsing then continues as script data through the next `</script>` in the document, which is the hydration block's. That block becomes inert text, `window.__MOE_FLIGHT_RUN__` is never assigned, and the report renders with no data. `JSON.stringify` does not escape `<`, so nothing else stops it.

The input is agent- and page-derived: `runJsonl` embeds `tool_result.text` verbatim, which for the web adapter is extracted page content. Any target page containing the literal `<!--<script` breaks the report for that run.

Reproduced with jsdom against the real template and the real escape-and-splice logic, script at `/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-ZKeown-Code-moe/4556b327-b63b-49d4-bbc6-78cd4f317e00/scratchpad/shard-025/repro-script-breakout.mjs`. The `</script` case is correctly neutralised; the comment case is not:

```
closing-tag payload
  scripts in doc: 3
  json node text length: 130
<!--<script payload
  scripts in doc: 1
  json node text length: 752
```

Script execution is not reachable, because closing the element from the double-escaped state needs a second `</script>` and those are escaped. So this is a content-controlled render break, not XSS. Fix: escape `<` as the JSON string escape `\u003c` throughout the payload, which is valid JSON, renders identically after `JSON.parse`, and closes both sequences at once.

### CR-196: The entire WebAdapter suite is gated behind `--project chrome` even though it never launches a browser, so CI never runs it
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/adapters/web/adapter.test.ts`
**Anchor:** the file's presence in `CHROME_SUITES` in `packages/flight/vitest.config.ts`, whose comment claims "each one calls `startChrome()`, which needs a browser on the box"
**Severity:** medium

Every test in this file either injects a stub session through the `chromeSession` option, constructs `WebAdapter` without calling `start()`, or exercises pure functions (`composeResult`, `toolDefinitions`). The only mentions of `startChrome` are the stub's recorded call name and assertions *about* that recording; there is no `beforeAll` that launches Chrome and no real CDP connection. The two `constructor → createSession threading` tests only call `createSession(...)` and `getActivePort()`, and `getActivePort` is a plain read of closure state — `chrome-ws-lib-isolation.test.ts` does the same thing and is already in the `unit` project.

Because `packages/flight`'s `test` script is `vitest run --project unit` and `.gitlab-ci.yml` contains no reference to `test:chrome`, `test:tmux` or `test:ffi`, roughly fifty stub-driven WebAdapter tests never run in CI. Among them are the side-trip tab depth cap, the `close()` teardown drain, the `install_at_depth_warning` events, and the `new_tab` URL-scheme guard that rejects `javascript:` — that last one is a security-relevant input check with no CI coverage at all. `AGENTS.md`'s "What CI runs, and what it does not" section lists the known gaps and does not mention any of flight's three gated projects, so the hole is also undocumented.

Fix: split this file so the stub-driven tests sit in the `unit` project and leave only genuinely browser-backed suites in `CHROME_SUITES`; the file currently contains none of the latter. Then bring `AGENTS.md`'s CI-gap list into line with the tree.

### CR-197: The bash-tool suite deletes a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead of restoring it
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/agent/bash-tool.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test "env passes through ANTHROPIC_API_KEY when set in parent" — `finally { delete process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; }`
**Severity:** medium

The test overwrites `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with `"sk-test-passthrough"` and then unconditionally deletes it, rather than restoring the previous value. Vitest's default pool reuses worker processes across test files, and `process.env` mutations survive that reuse (module isolation does not reset the process environment). Every other test in this package that touches the same variable saves and restores it — `test/qa/api/run.test.ts`, `test/qa/api/run-multi-pass.test.ts`, `test/qa/api/config-effective.test.ts` and `test/qa/models/validation.test.ts` all use the `const prev = …; if (prev === undefined) delete; else restore` shape. This file is the only one that does not.

The concrete victim is `test/qa/models/anthropic.test.ts`, whose live-API block is gated on `const skip = !process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;`. If it lands in the same worker after this file, the gate reads false and the live tests silently self-skip on a developer machine that does have a key — a green run with the provider seam unexercised, which is precisely the failure mode `vitest.config.ts`'s project split was written to eliminate.

Fix: capture `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` before the assignment and restore it (or delete only when it was previously absent), matching the pattern the rest of the suite already uses.

### CR-198: System-reminder prefix guard checks source text and covers one of five reminder literals
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/agent/system-reminder-prefix.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test "the grace-turn reminder literal in agent.ts opens with <SYSTEM-REMINDER>"
**Severity:** medium

The file's stated purpose is "If a future edit re-words the prefix in reflection.ts or agent.ts, these tests fail loudly instead of letting the UI silently fall back to UserMessagePanel." It does not deliver that for `agent.ts`. The assertion greps the file's raw source for a backtick-quoted template literal, and `agent.ts` has five `<SYSTEM-REMINDER>` literals: one backtick-quoted (the deadline grace-turn reminder) and four double-quoted — inside `buildStallWarning`, `buildStallForcedReminder`, `MAX_TOKENS_NUDGE`, and `EMPTY_RESPONSE_NUDGE`. I confirmed the counts by grep: one match for the backtick form, four for the double-quoted form.

All four uncovered literals reach `logger.logUserMessage(turns, extraUserText)` and therefore reach the UI's `isSystemReminder` check. Re-wording any of their prefixes leaves this suite green and silently demotes them to `UserMessagePanel`.

The check is also brittle in the false-failure direction: rewriting the one covered literal from `` `<SYSTEM-REMINDER>\n` `` to `"<SYSTEM-REMINDER>\n"` breaks the test with no behavioural change at all.

Fix: replace the source grep with value assertions, the way the sibling test does for `buildReflectionReminder` — export the four literals (or the two builder functions) from `agent.ts` and assert `isSystemReminder(...)` on each. That covers the real coupling and stops caring about quote style.

### CR-199: Fanout suite has no adversarial card-id case, leaving the write escape unguarded
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/fanout.test.ts`
**Anchor:** "Filenames come from the generated card's id (not a letter-suffix scheme)."
**Severity:** medium

The suite establishes exactly the dangerous property — that the model's `id` frontmatter determines the filename — and then only ever feeds it well-formed ids (`story-001-a`, `test-001-obs-1`, `test-002-fail-1`). Every fake client returns benign card text. There is no case where the model emits an id containing `..`, `/`, or an absolute path, so nothing in the suite fails when `writeCards` escapes `storiesDir`.

The file also has no traversal case for the route's own `:id` parameter, unlike `test/qa/api/results.test.ts` ("GET /api/results/:runId rejects path traversal") and `test/qa/api/run-sets.test.ts` ("rejects path-traversal attempts"), which is how the unvalidated `runId` read survives.

Fix: add a case whose fake client returns a card with `id: ../../../../escaped`, assert the response is a 4xx or that the card is skipped, and assert no file exists outside `storiesDir`. Add a `POST /api/fanout/..%2F..%2Fx/failure` case asserting 400.

### CR-200: Multi-pass API test builds a live network LLM client inside the "no network" unit project
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/run-multi-pass.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "test-key";` in "returns the new uniform response shape with N runIds"
**Severity:** medium

`runRoutes(config, broadcaster, undefined, registry, setBroadcaster, cancelTokens)` omits the 7th `clientFactory` argument, so the handler falls through to `createClient(model)` and builds a real Anthropic SDK client against the fake key. The route then fires the attempts detached and swallows their failures with `.catch(() => {})`, so the outbound HTTPS calls to the real API are invisible from the test. The `cli` adapter's `start()` does not fail first — it spawns `bash --norc --noprofile -i` and returns — so the agent loop reaches `client.chat()`. Three attempts in the first test, one in the second.

This contradicts the project contract stated in `vitest.config.ts`: "`unit` is the CI-safe set: no Chrome, no tmux, no network." It also re-creates the exact failure `test/qa/api/caps.test.ts` documents and fixed: "the sub-cap case is SUPPOSED to be accepted — which fires the run in the background, where it builds an LLM client... it made the suite intermittently red (observed once in ~15 runs). `runRoutes`' 7th parameter exists for exactly this."

The same tests also leak: four detached interactive `bash` processes and their `mkdtempSync` project roots, since the file has a `beforeEach` and no `afterEach` cleanup.

Not run (the brief forbids running suites). Fix: pass `caps.test.ts`'s `stubClientFactory` as the 7th argument in both tests, and add an `afterEach` that `rmSync`es `projectRoot`.

### CR-201: Restoring ANTHROPIC_API_KEY writes the string "undefined" when it was previously unset
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/run-multi-pass.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `} finally { process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = prev; }`
**Severity:** medium

`prev` is `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which is `undefined` on a box without the key — the normal CI case. Assigning `undefined` to a `process.env` property coerces it to the four-character string `"undefined"` rather than deleting the variable. I verified this: `node -e 'process.env.FOO = undefined; console.log(JSON.stringify(process.env.FOO), "FOO" in process.env)'` prints `"undefined" true`.

`process.env` is process-global and vitest reuses worker processes across test files, so after this file runs, later suites in the same worker see a truthy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. That flips behaviour rather than just leaking a value: code that branches on the key being present will construct a client and attempt a network call where it previously threw or skipped. `test/qa/api/config-effective.test.ts` does the restore correctly (`if (saved !== undefined) process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = saved; else delete process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY;`) — that is the pattern this file needs.

Fix: copy the `config-effective.test.ts` restore, or use vitest's `vi.stubEnv`/`unstubAllEnvs`.

### CR-202: Two API run tests fire real outbound HTTPS requests to api.anthropic.com
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/run.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"POST /api/run/:id returns 202 with uniform shape and registers by runId"`
**Severity:** medium

This test and `"POST /api/run/:id body chrome override wins over server default"` both set `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "test-key"` and then POST to the real `runRoutes` with no `clientFactory` and no `adapterFactory`. The route builds a real Anthropic SDK client via `createClientForProvider` and detaches `executeHttpRun`, which starts the real `CLIAdapter` (spawning a detached `bash --norc --noprofile -i`) and then enters the agent loop, whose first turn calls the SDK. With no `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set, that request goes to `https://api.anthropic.com`.

I reproduced the outbound call without touching Anthropic: driving `executeHttpRun` through the same `loadConfig`/`mergeRunConfig`/`createClientForProvider` path with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1` throws `Connection error.`, proving the SDK reaches the transport rather than short-circuiting earlier.

Both tests are in the `unit` project, which `vitest.config.ts` documents as "the CI-safe set: no Chrome, no tmux, no network." The tests then `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 100))` and `afterEach` deletes the project root, so the SDK's retry sequence and the detached bash both outlive the test that started them.

The comment in the test ("This will fail downstream (no real Chrome) but should still return 202") describes an intent the code does not implement — with `adapter: "cli"` there is no Chrome step to fail at.

Fix: pass the existing `clientFactory` seam on `runRoutes` and the `adapterFactory` seam on `executeHttpRun`, exactly as the sibling tests in the same file already do for the registry-ordering and screencast-gate cases.

### CR-203: Scenario id traversal is gated and tested on create only, not on read, update, delete or approve
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/scenarios.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"POST /api/scenarios rejects path traversal in id"`
**Severity:** medium

This suite has one traversal test, and it targets the one route that already has an `isSafePath` guard. The five other id-bearing handlers in `scenarioRoutes` (`GET /:id`, `PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id`, `POST /:id/approve`) and `POST /api/run/:id` pass the decoded path parameter straight to `findCard`, which has no guard. The test suite mirrors the production gap precisely, so the missing checks read as covered.

The concrete consequence is the finding above on `findCard`: I reproduced `GET /api/scenarios/..%2Fgarbage` returning a 500 after reading a file outside the stories directory. Nothing in this file would catch that, or catch a regression that removed the POST guard's siblings.

Fix: add a table-driven traversal case across every id-bearing route (encoded `..%2F`, `%2e%2e%2f`, and an absolute-looking id), asserting a 400 or 404 and, critically, that no read occurs outside the stories root.

### CR-204: Test pins the 500 handler echoing raw internal error text to HTTP clients
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/api/server.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"returns JSON 500 for unhandled route exceptions"`
**Severity:** medium

The only test in this file asserts `body.message).toBe("boom")`, locking in `app.onError` returning `err.message` verbatim to the caller. That is fine for the synthetic `throw new Error("boom")` route the test installs, and misleading about what real routes put in that field.

I reproduced a real leak through the same handler: `POST /api/scenarios` with `{"id":"a/b","title":"t"}` passes the `isSafePath` gate, fails inside `writeFileSync`, and returns `500 {"error":"internal","message":"ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/var/folders/.../T/repro-cardid-PIvDP7/.moe-flight/stories/a/b.md'"}` — the server's absolute filesystem layout, to an unauthenticated client on an all-interfaces bind.

The test as written would keep passing if the handler were changed to log the message and return a generic body only for non-synthetic errors, so it is not merely incomplete: it is the thing standing in the way of the fix.

Fix: assert the envelope shape (`error: "internal"`, no unbounded internal detail) rather than the echoed message, and change `app.onError` to log `err` server-side while returning a fixed client-facing message.

### CR-205: Secret-redaction test checks only the two API keys it already knows are redacted
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/cli/config-command.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"sdkEnv section only shows presence for secrets"`
**Severity:** medium

The test's name claims a general property of the `sdkEnv` block. Its body sets `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, then asserts the key reports `"set"` and the base URL passes through as `"https://custom"`. So it asserts, approvingly, that a value which routinely carries an embedded token is emitted verbatim, and it never touches `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `OPENAI_ORG_ID` or `OPENAI_PROJECT` at all.

`buildConfigOutput` is shared: the same block is served by `configEffectiveRoutes` over unauthenticated HTTP (see the high finding above). A test that pinned the name's actual claim — that no `sdkEnv` value capable of holding a credential appears in full — would have failed on the current implementation.

Fix: assert the property the name states. Set a credential-bearing `HTTPS_PROXY` such as `http://u:p@proxy:8080` plus both API keys, and assert the secret substring appears nowhere in either output format.

### CR-206: Soft-wrap test passes unchanged if soft-wrapping is removed entirely
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/cli/stream/pretty.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test `"assistant text longer than columns is soft-wrapped under the » glyph"`
**Severity:** medium

The test emits a `run_start` then a long `llm_response` at `columns: 24`, and selects "continuation" lines with `l.startsWith("  ") && l.trim().length > 0 && !l.includes("»")`. That filter also matches every line of the `run_start` banner, because `renderRunStart` writes each field as `  runId     r`, `  card      c`, and so on.

I ran the real renderer with those exact events and printed the selected set: six banner lines qualify, the longest at 13 characters of content, well inside the assertion's bound of 22. So all three assertions hold on banner lines alone. `/^» alpha/m` matches whether or not the text wrapped, `continuations.length > 0` is satisfied by the banner, and the per-line width check passes on short banner content. If `softWrap` degraded to the identity function the test would still be green.

Fix: restrict the filter to lines after the banner (slice the output at the blank line that closes `run_start`, or assert against the exact expected line array for that input the way the golden-fixture tests do).

### CR-207: Resolver timeout test never exercises the SIGKILL-after-grace stage its name claims
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/context/credential-tool.test.ts`
**Anchor:** test `"timeout: SIGTERM after timeout, then SIGKILL after grace"`
**Severity:** medium

The test asserts only `result.kind === "timeout"`, `elapsed < 3_500`, and `result.timeoutMs === 200`. Nothing observes which signal was sent, or in what order.

I ran `runResolver` against the `credential-resolver-slow.sh` fixture with `timeoutMs: 200` from the built module: kind `timeout`, elapsed 206 ms. The fixture is a plain `sleep 30`, so it dies on the SIGTERM that `signalResolver` sends to the process group and never reaches the grace timer. The assertion window of 3,500 ms is seventeen times the observed value and also admits the 2,200 ms path, so deleting the SIGTERM stage entirely would leave the test green.

The grace stage is the one that matters, and it is wholly unguarded. It is the only thing bounding `runResolver` for a resolver that traps SIGTERM — without the `killHandle` settle, `close` never arrives and the `fetch_credential` tool call hangs for the rest of the run. No fixture in the shard ignores SIGTERM.

Fix: add a fixture that traps and ignores SIGTERM, then assert `kind === "timeout"` with `elapsed >= timeoutMs + KILL_GRACE_MS`; and tighten the existing SIGTERM case to assert `elapsed < timeoutMs + KILL_GRACE_MS` so the two paths are distinguishable.

### CR-208: A fixture heading typo silently strips the story's acceptance criteria and disables the criteria contract

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/fixtures/stories/click-and-screenshot-pass.md`
**Anchor:** the heading `## Acceptance`
**Severity:** medium

`parseBody` in `story-card.ts` looks for the exact marker `## Acceptance Criteria`. This fixture writes `## Acceptance`, so the marker is not found, the two bullets are absorbed into `description`, and `acceptanceCriteria` comes back empty. That silently switches off the citation discipline the card exists to exercise: `parseReportCriteria` short-circuits with `if (acceptanceCriteria.length === 0) return { ok: true, value: [] }`, which is the only reason `web-form-post-nav.test.ts` can call `report("pass", ...)` with no `criteria` argument and still get `status: "pass"` instead of the `investigate` that `enforceCriteriaContract` would otherwise impose.

Reproduced with `node` against `dist/qa/format/story-card.js`: the card parses to `acceptanceCriteria: []` with both bullets and the stray heading left inside `description`. It is the only fixture with this typo; the other eight all use the full marker.

Fix: rename the heading to `## Acceptance Criteria` and pass `citeAll(card, "pass")` in the test, as the sibling web suites do. Separately, a card whose body contains a heading beginning `## Acceptance` that is not the exact marker should raise a warning rather than yield zero criteria, because this failure mode is invisible in the parsed card.

### CR-209: The profile-rotation cleanup can kill an unrelated process listening on port 9222

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/integration/chrome-profile-rotation.test.ts`
**Anchor:** the `finally` block's `await chrome.killChrome()`
**Severity:** medium

The test body calls `chrome.killChrome()` between the two profiles, and `killChrome` clears `state.chromeProcess` and resets `state.activePort` to `CHROME_DEBUG_PORT`, which defaults to 9222. If the body then throws anywhere at or after `startChrome(true, profileB)` — a failed rotation assertion is the expected way for this test to fail — the `finally` calls `killChrome()` again with no process handle. That path resolves a victim by port instead: `findPidOnPort(state.activePort)` shells out to `lsof -ti:9222 -sTCP:LISTEN`, then `killChrome` sends `/json/close` to the endpoint and `SIGTERM` to the pid. Port 9222 is also this project's own `defaultChrome` port, so the process most likely holding it is the operator's own debugging Chrome, which the test never started and which is closed and terminated as a side effect of a failing test.

Not reproduced; doing so requires launching Chrome, which this review does not do.

Fix: capture `chrome.getChromePid()` after each `startChrome` and, in the cleanup, only kill when the recorded pid is still the one the session owns. At minimum, guard the second `killChrome()` on `getChromePid()` being non-null.

### CR-210: The bc calculator e2e tests never invoke bc and pass on a machine without it

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/integration/cli-bc.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"fail: bc has no help command"`
**Severity:** medium

Both tests call `adapter.start("bc -q")`, but `CLIAdapter.start` ignores its argument: "Target is informational only — see describeTarget. We spawn bash, not the target." `bc` is reached only by the scripted `type` of `"bc -q\n"` into that shell, and nothing reads the shell's output back. The assertions are `result.status` and `result.scenario`, both taken from the scripted `report_result`. With `bc` absent the shell prints `command not found`, the typed `2+3` goes nowhere, and both tests stay green while claiming "bc performs arithmetic" and "bc has no help command". `tui-nano.test.ts` guards its dependency with `hasNano`; this file has no equivalent.

Fix: add a `spawnSync(["which", "bc"])` probe and `describe.skipIf`, then assert on the `read_output` tool results in `run.jsonl` for the strings `5` and `42` rather than on the scripted verdict.

### CR-211: The Chrome-unavailable guard reclassifies genuine assertion failures as skips

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/integration/helpers.ts`
**Anchor:** `isChromeUnavailable`
**Severity:** medium

`isChromeUnavailable(err)` returns true whenever `err.message` merely contains `ECONNREFUSED`, `No Chrome`, `chrome-ws-lib` or `adapter.start() timed out`. The three web suites wrap their `expect` calls inside the same `try` block that the guard protects, so a failing assertion whose received value quotes an adapter error is swallowed, the test prints `Skipping web e2e` and reports green. A tool result of `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222`, which is what the adapter produces when the CDP endpoint refuses mid-run, is exactly such a value.

Reproduced with `node` using vitest's own matcher stack from `@vitest/expect` plus `chai`: `expect("Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9222").toMatch(/^clicked /)` throws with message `expected 'Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1…' to match /^clicked /`, and `isChromeUnavailable` on that error returns true.

Fix: narrow the guard to the startup phase. Wrap only `adapter.start(...)` in the try that consults `isChromeUnavailable`, set a `skip` flag and return, and let the assertion block throw unconditionally. Excluding errors whose `name` is `AssertionError` would also work and is a one-line change.

### CR-212: The nano save test never checks that anything was saved

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/integration/tui-nano.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"pass: user can open, type, and save in nano"`
**Severity:** medium

The test writes `initial content` to a temp file, scripts `type` of `Hello from moe-flight!`, `press` of `Ctrl+O`, `press` of `Enter`, and then asserts `result.status` and `result.scenario`, which come from the scripted `report_result`. `afterEach` unlinks the temp file without ever reading it. Nothing verifies the save, and nothing verifies that `press` translated `Ctrl+O` into the right tmux key at all. This is the only test in the package that exercises `press` against a real terminal program: grep for the key names finds only this file, the story fixture, the TUI prompt, and the adapter itself, so a broken key translation table has no other guard.

Fix: after the run, read the temp file and assert it contains `Hello from moe-flight!`. That single assertion converts the test from plumbing smoke into a real check of `press`.

### CR-213: The TodoMVC e2e verdict assertions hold even when every browser tool fails

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/integration/web-todomvc.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"pass: user can add todo items"`
**Severity:** medium

The test scripts `type`, `press` and two `extract` calls, then a `report_result` with `status: "pass"`, and asserts only `result.status` and `result.scenario`. Both values come from the scripted `report_result` arguments, not from the browser. A failing tool call does not fail the run: the agent loop's executor catch turns any thrown error into `textResult("Error: " + message)` and continues, so the scripted verdict still lands. The extract results are never inspected, and the todo count the reasoning string claims to have checked is never read.

Reproduced with `node` against `dist/qa/agent/agent.js`: an adapter whose `executeTool` throws `no such element` for every tool still produced `status: "pass"`, `scenario: "todomvc-add-pass"`, so both assertions hold with the entire web adapter broken. The same shape governs `"fail: editing is not supported"` in this file and the single test in `web-smoke.test.ts`, which asserts only `result.status`.

Fix: assert on the evidence, the way `web-form-post-nav.test.ts` already does. Read `run.jsonl`, find the `tool_result` rows for the two `extract` calls, and assert the second one reports one item and the last reports two, plus `error: false` on every row.

### CR-214: The Anthropic key-validation test fails whenever a subscription token is exported

**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/models/validation.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `"Anthropic client throws clear error without API key"`
**Severity:** medium

The test deletes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and asserts `createAnthropicClient` throws. But `resolveAnthropicAuth` reads `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN || env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` first and returns `{ mode: "oauth" }` when either is present, so the constructor succeeds and the assertion fails. Anyone who has run `claude setup-token` and exported the result — the documented happy path for this tool and the normal state of a Claude Code shell — gets a red suite from a correct code base. This is the same class as the recent commit "test: unblock CI-run tests that assumed the developer's local environment"; CI passes only because no token is set there.

Reproduced with `node` against `dist/qa/models/anthropic.js`: with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` deleted and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` set, `createAnthropicClient("claude-sonnet-4-6")` returns normally.

Fix: delete all three variables inside the test and restore them in the `finally`. The same file's OpenAI case is safe because `createOpenAIClient` reads exactly one variable.

### CR-215: Random test ports turn a busy port into an uncaught exception that kills the worker
**File:** `packages/flight/test/qa/runtime/serve.test.ts`
**Anchor:** `freePort()` — "the test always binds with SO_REUSEADDR off, so a busy-loop here is unnecessary in practice"
**Severity:** medium

`freePort()` returns `40000 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 10000)` without ever
checking that the port is free, and the three tests in the file each roll their
own. The quoted justification is not a reason: `SO_REUSEADDR` governs rebinding a
port in `TIME_WAIT`, not whether some other process already owns it. The package
already ships the correct primitive, `pickFreePort()`, and the sibling
`serve-errors.test.ts` uses it.

The failure mode is disproportionate to the odds. `serve()` attaches no `error`
listener to the HTTP server, so a collision surfaces as an uncaught exception
rather than a rejected promise the test could fail on. I reproduced it by
calling `serve()` twice on one port: `UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION ... EADDRINUSE - listen
EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::45996`. Under vitest that aborts the
worker, taking unrelated suites in the same file down with it and reporting as an
unhandled error rather than a test failure. Note also that the chosen window
overlaps the macOS ephemeral range, so an unrelated outbound connection on the
box is enough to trigger it.

Fix: `await pickFreePort()` in place of `freePort()`, and give `serveViaNode` an
`error` handler so a bind failure reaches the caller instead of the process.

### CR-216: The committed `dist-static/static.html` template has no freshness gate and has already gone stale once
**File:** `packages/flight/ui/dist-static/static.html`
**Anchor:** commit 971e70d, "flight-ui: rebuild the committed dist-static bundle, which had gone stale"
**Severity:** medium

`renderRun` resolves its template through `staticReportTemplate()` to `<packageRoot>/ui/dist-static/static.html`, and that file is tracked. The root `.gitignore` ignores `dist/`, which covers `ui/dist/`, but not `dist-static/`, so the single-file bundle for the static report is a committed build artifact.
